## D-254: The Dashboard Carries Legacy's Logo As Its Favicon And On The Sign-In Page

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | Proposed 2026-09-15 in the pull request for #214 item 9; accepted when the repository owner merges it. |
| Decision | The port serves legacy's `logo.png`, byte for byte, at `/admin/_assets/logo.png`. The pages use it where legacy does. **The layout's and the sign-in page's `<head>`** name it as `<link rel="icon" type="image/png">` and `<link rel="apple-touch-icon">`, as `includes/layout.php:150-151` and `pages/login/page.php:67-68` do. **The sign-in page** shows it twice, with legacy's markup: `class="login-hero-logo" width="40" height="40"` with an empty `alt` in the hero brand (`page.php:79`), and `class="login-card-logo" width="48" height="48"` with the application's name as `alt` in the card head (`page.php:113`). Their styles already sit in the port's byte-copied `login.css`. **The sidebar** shows it beside the application's name, 28×28 with `class="logo-icon"` and the name as `alt`, as `dashboard/sidebar/view.php:15-18` does; the copied `sidebar.css` already carries that rule. `/admin/_assets/**` is already served without a session, and the sign-in page needs exactly that. |
| Divergences from legacy | **The URL.** Legacy's `workin_brand_logo_url()` (`includes/media.php:25-43`) points at the site root's `/logo.png`, with the host and a `?v=filemtime` query. The port serves the same file under its own assets path, with no query, like its stylesheets and scripts. **The file is legacy's 1024×1024 PNG unchanged** (1,364,971 bytes), including as the favicon, rather than a resized icon. Legacy serves that file, and a derived image would be a second artwork to keep in step. |
| Also in this change (#253) | `theDashboardShipsNoWebFontAndKeepsLegacysSystemStack` now fails for every way #251's review found a web font could come back. That covers a template linking a stylesheet from outside `/admin/_assets/`, a CSS `@import` or a Google Fonts host, an inline face, and a `font-family` other than legacy's stack in `style.css` or `login.css`, `inherit`, or the one emoji stack. It also covers the `font` shorthand, which carries a family too, and a `rel="stylesheet"` link however it is quoted. It matches in any letter case. The comments in `companies.jte` and `home.js` no longer give D-197's self-hosted typeface as their reason. |
| What does not change | Stylesheets, what any script does (`home.js` changes a comment only), security rules and every route. The sign-in page gains its two images and the sidebar its icon; no other page content changes. |
| Regression coverage | `AdminLayoutWiringTest.theLayoutAndTheSignInPageCarryLegacysLogo` pins three things: both heads' icon and touch-icon links, the sign-in page's two images with legacy's classes, sizes and `alt`, and `logo.png`'s sha256 as legacy's. `PlatformAdminAssetsExposureTest.theLogoIsServedWithoutASessionAsAPng` pins the file served without a session as `image/png` at full size. With `main`'s `layout.jte` and `login.jte` and no logo file, exactly those two failed of the two classes' 15 tests. The sign-in card losing its logo, and the file differing by one byte, each failed exactly the first. For #253, `theDashboardShipsNoWebFontAndKeepsLegacysSystemStack` failed alone for each of five mutants: the layout linking a Google Fonts stylesheet, `admin-extra.css` importing a font sheet, an inline `@FONT-FACE` in the sign-in page, a later sheet setting `body`'s `font-family`, and a `Cairo.WOFF2` file. Round 1's review added the sidebar image and two widenings. With `main`'s `sidebar.jte`, exactly `theLayoutAndTheSignInPageCarryLegacysLogo` failed. Two further mutants failed exactly the font test: `body { font: 14px/1.5 "Cairo", sans-serif; }` appended to `app-responsive.css`, and a single-quoted `rel='stylesheet'` linking a third-party sheet. The unquoted spelling cannot reach a test at all, because JTE answers `Unquoted HTML attribute values are not allowed: rel` and `:generateJte` fails. |
| Rollback | Revert the merge. Nothing is stored. |
| Corrected 2026-09-17 (#258) | **"A CSS `@import`" was narrower than it read.** The test matched an import only with whitespace after `@import`, and CSS needs none: `@import"https://cdn.example.com/cairo.css";` passed, and a sheet imported that way could bring back a face and a family that live outside `_assets`. The pattern now takes `@import` followed by a string or `url(` with or without whitespace, still refusing JTE's own `@import java...` directives. The test also reads CSS as a parser does, with comments removed and escapes decoded, so `@import/**/"…"` and `@\69mport "…"`, which Chromium both loads, count too. It matches each sheet and template both as written and as decoded, because a `/*` that opens no comment, such as the `/admin/_assets/**` in `layout.jte`'s JTE comment, would otherwise remove real text up to the next `*/`, a font included. A font brought back by script, a `<link>` injected at runtime or the `FontFace` API, is still not covered, as #251's review rounds recorded. |
| Corrected 2026-09-19 (#259) | **The icons are no longer the full file.** This corrects the "Decision" row, whose `<head>` sentence names `logo.png` as both icon links, as well as the "Divergences" row, which kept legacy's 1024×1024 PNG as the favicon and so put 1,364,971 bytes behind every page. The favicon and touch icon are now 32 and 180 pixel copies of it, `favicon-32.png` and `apple-touch-icon.png`, at the owner's choice of 2026-09-19. The sidebar and the sign-in page's two images still show `logo.png` byte for byte. D-266 records the copies and the assets' cache period. |
| Related | **#214** (item 9), **#253**, D-251, D-197, #258. |

## D-255: The Tables Follow Legacy's Actions Header And Its Character Clipping

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | Proposed 2026-09-16 in the pull request for #214 item 6; accepted when the repository owner merges it. |
| Decision | Two conventions legacy applies through its own helpers, which the port repeated by hand and lost. **The actions header** comes from one partial, `actionsHeader.jte`, which renders `tableStart()`'s markup: `<th class="col-actions" title="actions"><span class="sr-only">actions</span></th>` (`includes/layout.php:12-18`). Sixteen templates rendered a plain `<th>` with visible text, and four had the class without the label, so the column was 52px wide with text that clipped. Five more already carried the class and the label but wrote the markup themselves and left out legacy's `title`; they use the partial too, so all twenty-five headers come from one place. **The status badges** come from one partial too, `statusBadge.jte`, which is legacy's `badge()` (`layout.php:77-107`): one map from status to colour and label, an unknown status shown as itself in grey. Twenty-three badges across twenty-one pages picked their own colours, and pending was grey where legacy has it yellow, inactive red where legacy has it grey. Each page passes the status legacy passes at that same place, which is not always the obvious one: five org lists say `suspended` where the rest say `inactive` -- the same grey, a different word -- and the employee detail page says `1`/`0`, which legacy renders as yes and no. **The pager** now renders after the table card closes, as `tableEnd(); ?></div>` then `pagerHtml()` does (`requests/page.php:137-140`); nineteen of the twenty pagers, in seventeen pages, were drawn inside the card; `activities.jte` already had it right. **Long text** is cut where legacy cuts it: `ListDisplay.notes(text, max)` reproduces `hr_request_notes_display()` (`includes/hr_list_helper.php:495-506`) -- PHP's `trim()`, an em dash when nothing is left, and otherwise `mb_substr(0, max)` with a horizontal ellipsis. The count is in code points, because `mb_strlen` counts characters while `String.length()` counts UTF-16 units. Each cell keeps the whole text in its `title`, as legacy's does. |
| Where each length comes from | 60: requests' notes and reply (`requests/page.php:128-129`), an asset's text (`assets/page.php:165`) and a decision's body (`administrative_decisions/page.php:177`). 50: a complaint's message (`complaints/page.php:186`) and a notification's body (`notifications/page.php:207`). 40: a penalty's reason (`penalties/page.php:182`), a complaint's reply (`:187`), and an advance's reason and rejection reason (`advances/page.php:212-213`). |
| Divergences from legacy | **The asset text** was not clipped at all before, and its cell keeps the port's `bold` class; only the clipping and the `title` are added. **The FAQ list** is legacy's one `mb_strimwidth()` table (`faqs/page.php:131-132`), not an `hr_request_notes_display()` one, so it gets its own helper: `ListDisplay.strimwidth()` counts the ellipsis inside the width, trims nothing, and leaves empty text empty. The port also showed the answer in the cell's `title` there, which legacy does not; that is gone. |
| What does not change | What any column contains, the order of the columns, and the row menus and their colours: those already matched legacy. The badges and the pager did not, and this change fixes both -- an earlier draft of this entry claimed otherwise, which #257's first review round disproved. |
| Regression coverage | `ListDisplayTest` holds both helpers to legacy's: the em dash for nothing, what fits shown whole, the cut with its ellipsis, Arabic counted by letters, an emoji never split, PHP's trim set rather than Java's, and, for the FAQ cut, the ellipsis counted inside the width with nothing trimmed. `AdminTableConventionsTest` reads the templates and fails closed: `everyActionsHeaderComesFromTheSharedPartial`, `everyLongTextColumnCutsWhereLegacyCutsIt` (a call it cannot parse is a failure, not a skip), `everyClippedCellKeepsTheWholeTextInItsTitle`, `noColumnClipsByWidthWhereLegacyCutsTheText`, `everyStatusBadgeComesFromTheSharedPartial`, `theStatusBadgeCarriesLegacysColourAndLabelForEveryStatus`, which checks the map status by status against legacy's, `noPagerSitsInsideItsTableCard`, `everyBadgePassesTheStatusLegacyPassesAtThatPlace`, which compares the status each page hands the partial with legacy's own argument at that call site, and `everyLabelTheStatusBadgeCanAskForResolves`, which covers the labels the partial builds at runtime and the template key gate therefore no longer sees. With round 1's `requests.jte`, exactly the badge and pager gates failed. Six mutants each failed exactly the test that pins them: pending painted grey, a cell losing its `title`, the FAQ cut taking 40, a clip written without its length, a pager put back inside its card, and the ellipsis counted outside the width. Round 2 added three more cases, each failing exactly the gate that pins it: a page passing `inactive` where legacy passes `suspended`, the detail page passing a status word where legacy passes `1`/`0`, and a label dropped from the catalogue. After the change, 685 tests in 62 classes under `com.workin.backend.platformadmin` passed. |
| Rollback | Revert the merge. Nothing is stored. |
| Corrected 2026-09-17 (#261, #260) | **The badges legacy draws were not all drawn.** The employee detail page printed a request's and an advance's raw status and a penalty's applied-to-payroll flag as "Active"/"Inactive" text, where legacy draws `badge()` (`employees/detail.php:95`, `:102`, `:109`); D-262 draws them. `everyBadgePassesTheStatusLegacyPassesAtThatPlace` checks the status each badge the port draws is given; it cannot see a badge legacy draws and the port does not, which is each page's own end-to-end test. **The complaints badge has no legacy counterpart.** Legacy always renders an inline status select there (`complaints/page.php:195-205`) and never calls `badge()`; the port's badge is its read-only stand-in for a viewer who cannot write, and the gate's Javadoc now says so. **Three gates could miss a future edit (#260).** The status gate read a badge's literals in source order, so a negated condition passed: `everyTwoWayBadgeShowsItsOnStatusWhenItsConditionHolds` now requires each of the nineteen two-way badges to be un-negated with its on status first, and `AdminBranchesEndToEndTest` renders an active and a suspended branch and reads each badge's colour and label. `everyStatusBadgeComesFromTheSharedPartial` flagged only a computed colour, so a fixed-colour badge labelled with a status passed; it now also flags a span whose class holds `badge` and a `badge-…` colour, wherever the class sits among its attributes, and whose label is a status, gender, method, role or yes/no key, including one built from its prefix as `"status_" + row.status()` or `"status_%s"`. A computed colour is flagged when the attribute itself names the badge class, as text or as a string inside the expression: `badge ${…}`, `badge-${…}`, an expression beside a `badge` class, or `${ok ? "badge badge-green" : "badge badge-red"}`. The gate reads each tag and its class to the `>` and `"` that close them outside any expression. A class held in a variable and printed as `class="${cls}"` names no badge there and is not caught. `everyClippedCellKeepsTheWholeTextInItsTitle` read one line at a time, so a cell wrapped across lines dropped out; it now reads across lines and fails unless it read a cell for every `ListDisplay.notes(` call. |
| Related | **#214** (item 6), D-209, D-254, #261, #260, D-262. |

## D-256: The Attendance Page Formats Its Cells As Legacy Does

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | Proposed 2026-09-16 in the pull request for #214 item 5 (the attendance page's part); accepted when the repository owner merges it. |
| Decision | The attendance page showed stored values where legacy formats them. The helpers are now in `AttendanceDisplay`, which already held the day-name cell, and the page uses them cell for cell (`attendance/page.php:202-206, 248-250`). **The date** is `hr_format_attendance_date_cell()`: the day, the month's name and the year, "5 مارس 2026" in Arabic and PHP's `j F Y`, "5 March 2026", otherwise. The port showed `2026-03-05`. **The times** are `hr_format_attendance_time_cell()`, `H:i`, in `dir="ltr"` cells, and an open shift's check-out is legacy's muted dash. The port showed the whole stored `2026-03-05 08:07:09`. **Worked hours** in the punch list are `payroll_format_attendance_hours()`, signed and zero-padded, `08:05`; the port wrote `8:05`. **The summary's hours** are `payroll_format_duration_ar()`, "2 ساعة و 5 دقيقة", with nothing or less shown as "0 دقيقة"; the port wrote `2:05`. **Overtime** is `payroll_render_overtime_delta_badge()`, a count of minutes in `att-overtime-badge--plus` or `--minus`, or a muted dash for none; the port wrote a coloured `±H:MM`. **The wrapper**: legacy's attendance and payroll pages are `class="content payroll-page hr-page"`, and the port gave both only `hr-page`. The toolbar and table-card rules `app-ui.css` writes for `.hr-page` as well already applied, and `payroll-pages.css`'s own table-card rule is overridden on both pages by `hr-pages.css`, which loads after it at the same specificity, as in legacy. What the wrapper brings in is the overtime badge, and the payroll detail card's one line per cell, at 12px, in a table at least 1400px wide, which `.table-wrap` scrolls sideways. (Corrected by #264: this sentence first said the card's background, clipping and spacing came in too.) The payslip table also lacked the `payroll-detail-card` class those last rules select (`payroll/page.php:241`), and has it now. The summary's day counts and the overtime cell take legacy's `col-center`, and the summary's row number and the punch list's weekday lose a `text-muted` legacy does not give them. |
| How the formats were established | Legacy's own functions, extracted from `table_ui.php` and `payroll_list_helper.php` unchanged and run under PHP 8.3 against dates, times and minute counts at every boundary (a bare date, `T` for the space, no seconds, a fraction, padding, the zero date, an impossible date; zero, negative, 59, 60, 61 and 6000 minutes). `AttendanceDisplayTest` asserts those outputs. Month and day names are literal arrays, as legacy's are: PHP's `F` is always English, and a JVM locale's CLDR names are neither guaranteed to be the same words nor stable across JDKs. |
| Divergences from legacy | **A shortfall keeps its minus sign.** Legacy prints the bare count and leaves the grey of `--minus`, against the yellow of `--plus`, to say it is a shortfall; the port prints "-30 دقيقة", so the column does not rest on colour alone. The port's own cell was red before; legacy's grey badge replaces it. **A date with a zero part is a dash.** Such values are stored: under `sql_mode=''` the API writes an unparseable check-out as `0000-00-00 00:00:00` (`LegacyAttendanceStore`), and a zero month or day is kept as written (`LegacyJdbcValues`). PHP rolls them over -- the zero date is "30 November -0001", "Tuesday" and "00:00", and `2026-00-10` is "10 December 2025" -- and the port shows a dash in the date, day and time cells. The comment on `dayName` that said PHP parses a zero date to nothing was wrong, and is gone. **Kept on purpose:** legacy's `و` joins hours and minutes in English too, and its units are singular ("2 hour"); both are what legacy renders. |
| Not in this change | Money, with its thousands separators and currency, and penalty day words -- the rest of #214 item 5 -- follow separately. The employee detail page's attendance sub-table shows whole timestamps where legacy shows `HH:MM`, and is tracked with that page's badges in #261. |
| Regression coverage | `AttendanceDisplayTest` holds each helper to the output legacy's own functions printed under PHP 8.3: the month names in both languages and all twelve in Arabic, `HH:MM` with its zero, what `hr_parse_datetime()` accepts (`T` for the space, no seconds, a fraction, surrounding whitespace) and what it refuses (a bare date, nothing), a date with a zero part -- the zero date, a zero month, a zero day -- as a dash, the weekday from Sunday, signed zero-padded hours, the duration in words with nothing or less as "0 دقيقة", and overtime in minutes with the shortfall's sign. `AdminAttendanceEndToEndTest.theRowsCarryLegacysDateTimeAndHoursFormats` renders the page over three employees, one over eight hours, one under and one exactly, and checks the wrapper, each cell's format, both badge classes with their text and the muted dash. `AdminLayoutWiringTest.everyPageWrapsItsContentInLegacysClasses` compares every page's `.content` classes with legacy's page by page, and fails on a page it has no entry for. With `main`'s `attendance.jte` and `payroll.jte`, exactly the end-to-end test and the wrapper gate failed. Nine mutants each failed exactly the test that pins them: payroll losing its wrapper, a shortfall painted with the plus class, March given the Levantine name a locale could supply, the time's hour unpadded, no fallback for a value without seconds, the weekday counted from Monday, worked hours unpadded, a negative duration not read as nothing, and the shortfall's sign dropped as legacy drops it. After round 1's fixes, the payslip table without `payroll-detail-card` failed exactly `AdminPayrollEndToEndTest.theBatchDetailRendersItsPayslipsAndTotals`, and a lenient parse that rolls a zero part over as PHP does failed exactly `aDateWithAZeroPartIsADashRatherThanLegacysRollover`. |
| Rollback | Revert the merge. Nothing is stored. |
| Related | **#214** (item 5), D-255, #261. |

## D-257: Money, Advances And Penalty Days Print As Legacy Prints Them

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | Proposed 2026-09-16 in the pull request for #214 item 5 (money and penalty day words); accepted when the repository owner merges it. |
| Decision | Four pages printed stored numbers where legacy formats them. **Payroll** (`payroll/page.php`): every payslip amount goes through `$fmtPay`, `number_format($v, 0)`, now `PayrollDisplay.money()` over `PhpMath.numberFormat` -- whole pounds grouped in threes, and a missing value printed as legacy's `?? 0` rather than a dash. Overtime hours are `number_format($v, 1)`. The batch list's net carries legacy's literal " ج.م" (`:203`), and the batch totals use `$fmtPay` (`:237-239`). The payslip's total deductions and net take legacy's emphasis, `text-red bold` and `bold text-green` (`:307-308`). **Advances** (`advances/page.php:209-210`): the amount and the remaining amount are `number_format(…, 0)`, and the remaining amount is a red cell while any is owed and a green one once none is, where the port drew a blue badge. **Penalties** (`penalties/page.php:181, :231`): the days are `dashboard_penalty_days_option_label()` -- "ربع يوم", "نص يوم", "يوم", "N أيام", else the number -- in a `text-red bold` cell where the port drew a grey badge, and in both day pickers; the value a form posts back is still the number. **Home** (`index.php:320-322`): the salary totals are `home_format_money()`, which appends `__('currency_egp')`; `HomeSummary`'s comment said legacy appends nothing. |
| How the formats were established | `dashboard_penalty_days_option_label()` and `number_format()` at 0 and 1 places were run under PHP 8.3 at their boundaries (the tolerance around a quarter, a half and one; zero; non-whole values; half-way amounts; nulls through `?? 0`). `PenaltyDaysLabelTest` and `PayrollDisplayTest` assert those outputs. `PhpMath.numberFormat` is the corpus-measured whole-pound formatter and is reused unchanged. |
| Kept as legacy has it | The payroll list's currency is the literal " ج.م" in both languages, as `:203` writes it; the home page's is the translated key, as `home_format_money()` uses it. |
| Also in this change | D-256's sentence on the `payroll-page` wrapper is corrected (#264): `hr-pages.css` overrides `payroll-pages.css`'s table-card rule on both pages, so the wrapper brings in only the overtime badge and the payroll detail card's rules. |
| Not in this change | The employee detail page's figures and its literal " ج.م" (`employees/detail.php:77-78, 109, 120-126`) go with that page's other gaps in #261. The payroll batch view's totals are a stats grid in legacy and a one-row table here, and its payslip rows lead with a row number and the employee code; both are layout rather than formatting. A quarter-day penalty may not survive the `decimal(5,1)` column at all (#263). |
| Regression coverage | `PenaltyDaysLabelTest` and `PayrollDisplayTest` hold the helpers to legacy's output: the three words, the tolerance around them, whole numbers counted in days with zero included, other values as the bare number, the form's posted value unchanged; whole pounds grouped in threes with halves away from zero, a numeric string through `(float)`, a missing value as `0`, and overtime hours always to one place. End to end: `AdminPenaltiesEndToEndTest.theDaysReadAsLegacysWords` renders the list cell and both pickers; `AdminAdvancesEndToEndTest.theAmountsAreWholePoundsAndTheRemainingIsColouredByWhetherItIsOwed` renders an owed and a repaid advance; `AdminPayrollEndToEndTest.theBatchListRenders` checks the list's net with its currency and `theBatchDetailRendersItsPayslipsAndTotals` the totals, the overtime hours and the payslip's emphasis; and `PlatformAdminFullFlowTest.theCompleteAdministrativeJourney` requires the currency on exactly the three salary cards. With `main`'s four templates, exactly those five end-to-end tests failed. Eight mutants each failed exactly the tests that pin them: a repaid advance counted as owed, payroll money ungrouped, overtime hours to no places, one day falling through to the day count, the tolerance narrowed below legacy's, the net salary card without its currency, the batch list's net without its currency, and the payslip's net without its green. After round 1, the test reads each picker on its own, since both render the same options: the edit window's picker reverted to bare numbers, and the add form's, each failed `theDaysReadAsLegacysWords`. |
| Rollback | Revert the merge. Nothing is stored. |

## D-258: Every Terminal Path Lands In The Monolith, Through An Agent, A File Or A Push

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | Proposed 2026-09-16 in the pull request that adds `devices-agent/`; accepted when the repository owner merges it. The owner chose, in chat on 2026-09-16: keep hr-platform's device module and retire the standalone proof of concept (`poc-fingerprint-devices/workin-punch-gateway`, never in version control); support old and new terminals; a Python agent shipped as a Windows executable; and a production-database mode for the site visit. Renumbered from D-257, which #265 took first on `main`. |
| Decision | **One ingestion path, four ways in.** A ZKTeco terminal that pushes keeps the D-164 receiver. A terminal that cannot push is read on its own LAN by an on-premises agent, which submits ATTLOG lines to `POST /api/v1/device-agents/punches` with a bearer token; the platform parses them with the receiver's parser and stores them with the receiver's dedup key, so a punch that arrives twice by two paths is one row. A USB export is imported from `/admin/devices` (up to 1 MB) or through the agent. `device_punches.delivered_via` (`PUSH`, `AGENT`, `FILE`) records which path came first. **Agents** are a new table, `device_agents`: one company each, token stored as SHA-256 with its last four characters for recognition, issued and revoked by the platform administrator, and authenticating nothing once deactivated. Their endpoint has its own security chain and flag (`app.devices.agents.enabled`, default off), and an agent can submit only for an active device already allocated to its own company -- anything else answers the same `404`. **Platform-mediated allocation** is the new `/admin/devices` page: the administrator allocates an unclaimed serial to a branch, choosing the vendor (`zkteco`, and now `hikvision`), with the same validation as the tenant claim and an audit row. **The agent is not built on pyzk.** pyzk is GPL-2.0, the agent ships as an executable handed to customers, and pyzk's attendance read first fetches the terminal's user table, device passwords included. The agent carries its own 4370 client, which can send only read commands; pyzk is used in a test that cross-checks the emulator, and is excluded from the build. **The edge serves the device name over plain HTTP** as well as HTTPS, without redirecting: the design accepts HTTP-only firmware (specification §8), and Caddy's automatic redirect made every such terminal unable to deliver. |
| Why not the proof of concept | It ran on PostgreSQL beside a MariaDB production (ADR-0017), owned tenants as UUIDs unrelated to `companies`, had no pairing to attendance and no review history, and was not in version control. Its agent design (spool as cursor, deliver only on 200, serial check, Hikvision time-window cursor) and its field kit were carried over and rewritten against this module's contract. |
| Schema | `phase1_extensions.sql` creates fifteen tables. A database provisioned with the earlier fourteen takes `upgrade_device_agents_and_delivery.sql`, whose every statement is guarded and whose result has the same `SHOW CREATE TABLE` as a fresh apply (measured on MariaDB 10.6 and 11.8, including a table with rows). `verify_phase1_tables.sql` names that state `PRE-AGENTS`, and `Phase1SchemaCheck` now also reports a missing `device_punches.delivered_via`, because a `--force` re-apply would add the table and leave every device insert failing. |
| Not in this change | A Hikvision **push** receiver: the agent reads Hikvision over ISAPI, and the site-visit recorder captures what a Hikvision pushes, which is the evidence a receiver needs first. Unclaim, transfer and replace-device (R-042 stays open). Pairing punches into attendance has no caller yet (unchanged), so nothing here writes attendance. The Windows executable is built on a Windows machine (`packaging/windows/build-exe.ps1`); CI runs the agent's tests only. |
| Unverified until a site visit | Which of a ZKTeco record's two codes is the in/out key (`in_out_field`, default `punch`, the SDK's 40-byte layout); a USB export's column order; Hikvision's attendance event codes (default 1, 38, 75); whether a firmware splits an upload above the 5,000-record cap. Each has a step and a falsifier in `docs/devices/field-visit-runbook.md`. |
| Regression coverage | `DeviceAgentEndToEndTest` (real MariaDB): an agent's punches stored against its company's device with the employee resolved, re-delivery stored once, the same scan pushed and read as one row credited to the push, another company's, an unknown and an inactive serial answered identically with nothing stored, no token, a malformed one and a revoked one refused, an unreadable line quarantined, a batch above the cap refused whole, a USB delivery marked `FILE` and an unknown delivery refused, and a heartbeat that refreshes only its own devices and turns an unknown serial into a sighting. `AdminDevicesEndToEndTest`: allocation with its history and audit rows, a second allocation refused with a message and no audit row, a token rendered once and stored as a digest, revoked, and a USB export imported twice and stored once. `Phase1SchemaCheckTest`: a pre-agents database reported and repaired by the upgrade, which is harmless when re-run. `DevicesModuleIsolationTest`: every agent-surface bean gated by its flag. The agent: 40 unit tests, and pyzk reading the emulator exactly as the agent's client does over TCP and UDP, with and without a Comm Key. `scripts/devices-lab.sh simulate` runs all four paths against the local stack. |
| Rollback | Turn `APP_DEVICES_AGENTS_ENABLED` off, which removes the agent surface. Reverting the merge leaves the fifteenth table and the column in place, harmlessly; removing them is in `docs/operations/provisioning-phase1-tables.md`. |
| Related | D-164, D-165, ADR-0006, R-023, R-042, #12. |

## D-259: A Row Action's Window Is Legacy's Modal, Not A Native Dialog

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | Proposed 2026-09-16 in the pull request for #214 item 7; accepted when the repository owner merges it. Supersedes D-198's choice of a native `<dialog>` for row actions; the rest of D-198 stands. |
| Decision | `rowDialog.jte` renders legacy's window, `<div class="modal-bg"><div class="modal">` with its `.modal-close` button, an `h2` title and a `form-footer` (the markup of `requests/page.php:143-163` and `advances/page.php:270`), instead of `<dialog class="row-dialog">`. `row-dialog.js` still fills the one window per page from the row's `data-dialog-*` values and announces `row-dialog:filled`, then opens it with legacy's `open` class. `crud.js` closes it on the close button and the backdrop, as it does every other modal, and `modal-a11y.js` gives it Escape, the Tab trap, focus on the first field and focus back to the opener. A window opened from a row's ⋮ menu returns focus to that row's ⋮ button: `row-dialog.js` focuses it before opening, because the menu item itself has just been put back inside its closed menu. Each field sits in its own `.form-row`, its label beside its control as legacy writes them (`<div class="form-row"><label for>…</label><input id>`, a checkbox inside its label), its submit button takes legacy's colour -- green to approve a request, red to reject a request, an advance or a company -- and the complaint-reply and company-reject windows carry the Cancel legacy gives them, beside Save (`complaints/page.php:240`, `companies/page.php:288`). That Cancel is a plain grey button that `row-dialog.js` closes the window on, not `.modal-close`: the stylesheets position that class as the ×, absolutely, and in the sticky footer it lay over Save, so a tap meant to save closed the window and lost what was typed. All fourteen row windows change at once -- advances (reject, edit), assets, attendance, companies and company detail (reject), complaints (reply), FAQs (category, item), leave balances, penalties, phone countries, and requests (approve, reject) -- because they all come from the one partial. |
| Why | #214 item 7. Legacy draws every window as `.modal-bg > .modal` -- 43 across `dashboard/pages` and `dashboard/includes` at `505004f`, 24 opened by script and 19 rendered already open by the server, such as the company reject form -- including the decisions the port drew as dialogs (`requestDecisionModal`, `advanceDecisionModal`, `complaintModal`). The port drew the add form in legacy's modal and the edit or decision for the same row in a native dialog, so one page opened two different windows. D-198 chose the native dialog for its focus trap, Escape, backdrop and the inertness of the page behind it. `modal-a11y.js` supplies the first three for legacy's markup; inertness it does not -- the Tab trap keeps the keyboard in the window, and `aria-modal` tells assistive technology, but the page behind is not made inert. That loss is accepted for one kind of window across the dashboard. |
| Also fixed | **The table card was a containing block.** `app-ui.css` animates `.data-table-card` with `appFadeUp`, whose kept `transform` makes the card the containing block of every fixed element inside it. Legacy escapes that by writing its modals after the card; here the add modals and nine of the row windows sit inside it, so they were laid out against the card -- off-centre, scrolling the page on open, and on a short list with the title and × above the top of the document. The fix `admin-extra.css` already made for `.content` (the fade kept, the translate dropped) now covers the card too, under `app-ui.css`'s own selectors. The add modals on five of those pages -- advances, assets, attendance, leave balances and penalties -- and on notifications had the same fault before this change. **Three reject buttons were unstyled:** `btn-danger` is defined by no stylesheet. `modal-a11y.js` meant to focus a window's first field rather than its close button, and did not. Its selector put `.modal` and a space in front of a comma-separated list and `:not(.modal-close)` after it, which scoped only the first and last alternatives, so the unscoped `button:not([disabled])` matched the close button that opens every window. Every modal on the dashboard opened with focus on its ×. The selector is now built alternative by alternative. **The sticky footer covered the last field.** `admin-extra.css` stuck the footer at `bottom: 0`, with margins cut for 28px of padding where `app-ui.css` gives the modal 26px, and 20px on a phone. A sticky element stops short of its scroller's padding, so on every modal, add modals included, the footer rode 2 to 8px over the last field, and a click on that edge landed on the footer. It now sticks at the modal's own bottom edge, with margins that match the padding. |
| Divergences from legacy | **The subject line.** The window keeps the port's line naming the row the action is about (`.row-dialog__subject`), which legacy's windows do not have. Legacy names the row in the window's title instead, where the port's title is the action alone: the employee in a request's or an advance's decision, with the advance's amount (`requests/assets/requests-actions.js:24-28`, `advances/assets/advance-actions.js:29-40`), the complaint's number and submitter in a reply (`complaints/assets/complaint-form.js:29-32`), and the company in a reject. It also shows the complaint's text in a preview block above the reply (`complaints/page.php:223`), which the port does not. **The complaint Cancel.** Legacy's carries `.modal-close`, so legacy's stylesheet draws it in the ×'s corner, not in the footer (`complaints/page.php:240`, `style.css:190`); the port's sits beside Save. **Field width.** A `datetime-local` field, attendance's check-in and check-out, keeps its own width, as it does in legacy, whose stylesheet sizes only the other input types to the row. **Keyboard.** Legacy's request, advance and complaint scripts focus the comment, reason or reply field as their window opens (an advance's approval focuses Approve instead; `requests-actions.js:37`, `advance-actions.js:60-64`, `complaint-form.js:39`). Focus on the first field in the other row windows, and in all of them Escape, the Tab trap and focus back to the opener, are `modal-a11y.js`'s; no legacy window has Escape, a Tab trap or focus back to the opener. **Wording.** A request decision's field is labelled with the port's `reply`, where legacy's reads `decision_reply` and `(optional)` and carries a placeholder (`requests/page.php:153-155`). **The company Cancel.** Legacy's is a link back to `companies.php`, because its reject form is rendered already open by the server; the port's reject window is opened by script, so its Cancel closes it, which leaves the admin on the same list. **Placement.** The windows stay inside their table cards, where legacy writes them after the card; the card no longer contains fixed elements, so they lay out as legacy's do. |
| Not in this change | Legacy often reuses one window for a page's add and edit (`crudOpenEdit`), where the port keeps a separate edit window beside the add modal. They now look alike; merging them is a per-page change with its own forms and tests. |
| Regression coverage | In the browser, with no stack (`deploy/e2e/tests/row-dialog.spec.js`), the real `crud.js`, `row-dialog.js`, `modal-a11y.js` and `style.css` run on a page shaped like `rowDialog.jte`. The spec checks that the window is hidden until a row opens it; each row fills it, with the checkbox and the reset between rows; the fill is announced before it opens; Enter submits through Save while the close button submits nothing; Escape and the backdrop close it and a click inside does not; opening focuses the first field and closing returns focus to the row; and a current-only option is enabled only for its row. `emp-picker.spec.js` runs the picker inside the same window. `AdminRowDialogButtonsTest` pins the template's shape: legacy's `.modal-bg > .modal`, one submit button, a `type="button"` close button and no `<dialog>`. The end-to-end tests for requests, attendance and the active checkbox slice the rendered window from its `.modal-bg`. With `main`'s `row-dialog.js`, 13 browser tests failed: every row-dialog test and the four emp-picker tests that open a window. With `main`'s `modal-a11y.js`, exactly the two focus tests failed. A window not reset between rows failed exactly the checkbox-carry-over test, and a fill announced after opening failed exactly the announcement test. With `main`'s `rowDialog.jte`, `AdminRowDialogButtonsTest` and seven end-to-end tests across requests, attendance and the active checkbox failed. A close button made a submit button failed exactly `AdminRowDialogButtonsTest`. After #266's first review round, the spec also renders a real list page: the layout's stylesheets in the layout's order, a table card of 40 rows and of 2 holding the window, opened from a row's ⋮ menu. It asserts the backdrop is exactly the viewport, the window's title and Save are on screen, opening does not scroll the page, a click over the topbar closes it, and focus returns to the row's ⋮ button. With the card still transformed, exactly the two card tests failed; without the focus hand-off, exactly the ⋮ test. After the second round, the same page carries a footer Cancel beside Save at 1280×720 and at 390×844, and the spec asserts the two do not overlap, a click at Save's centre submits, and Cancel closes the window without submitting. With that Cancel given `.modal-close`, and separately with `row-dialog.js` not closing on it, exactly those two tests failed. `AdminRowDialogButtonsTest` also requires that no footer button in `rowDialog.jte` takes `.modal-close`, and with it put back exactly that test failed. `AdminRowDialogButtonsTest` also requires every label in a row window to sit in a `.form-row` and every submit variant to be a button class a stylesheet defines: a complaint field put back outside its row, and `btn-danger` put back on the advance reject, each failed exactly its gate. After the third round, that page also carries a reply window, and a window longer than the screen, at 1280×720 and at 390×844. The spec asserts that the last field ends above the footer and its bottom edge is its own, that Save stays in view before and after scrolling, and that the stuck footer ends at the window's edge. With the footer CSS as it was, exactly the two 1280 tests failed, and so did the same two with the footer stuck at `bottom: 0` behind the matched margins; with the phone's offset not following its padding, exactly the 390 long-window test failed. `AdminRowDialogButtonsTest` now requires each field to be its own `.form-row` with a label `for` its control (a checkbox inside its label), the footer Cancel to carry `data-dialog-cancel`, which `row-dialog.js` closes on, and exactly the three windows legacy gives a Cancel to pass one. With the six windows' markup as it was, and separately with one label wrapping its control again, exactly the form-row test failed; without the hook, exactly the shape test; without the complaint's Cancel, exactly the Cancel test. Afterwards, with `main` merged in, 208 Java tests in 18 classes and all 71 stack-free browser tests passed. |
| Rollback | Revert the merge. Nothing is stored; every form posts what it posted before. |
| Corrected 2026-09-17 (#270, first part) | **The containing-block fix's stylesheet order is tested.** The rule in `admin-extra.css` overrides `app-ui.css` only by loading after it, and `row-dialog.spec.js` and `nav-drawer.spec.js` listed the layout's stylesheets by hand, so reordering `layout.jte`'s links would have kept every test green. Both specs now read the links from `layout.jte`. **The companies form's ids.** `companies.jte` wrote `co_title` and `co_size` on its toolbar filters, as legacy does, and again on its add and edit form, so the form's labels pointed at the toolbar's selects. The form's are now `co_title_id` and `co_size_id`, and `AdminTemplateIdsTest` fails on any admin template writing a literal id twice. The add modals' markup, the rest of #270, follows separately. |
| Corrected 2026-09-17 (#270, second part) | **The add windows write one field to a row.** The "Not in this change" row said a page's add and edit windows "now look alike". On the FAQ and phone-country pages that was false: their add modals put several label-wrapped controls in one `.form-row`, which renders them as narrow controls inline beside their text, and the guide-video, notification and banner add modals did the same. All six now write legacy's rows, a label naming its control and then the control, one to a `.form-row`, with a checkbox inside its label as legacy's is. They take legacy's field order, titles (`add_country`, `add_faq_category`, `add_faq_question`, `add_banner`, `send_notification`) and Save label (`faqs/page.php:153-217`, `phone_countries/page.php:95-138`, `guide_videos/page.php:91-123`, `banners/page.php:111-232`, `notifications/page.php:222-300`). The country form's length starts at 11, the question form asks for a category instead of preselecting the first, and the banner form pairs its fields in legacy's `.banner-form-grid` with its hint in `.form-hint`. `AdminRowDialogButtonsTest` applies the row windows' rule to every `.modal-bg` window a page writes itself, with an id or without, reading the window to its closing tag whether its form sits inside it or around it, and counts every `modal-bg` the templates write, so a window it cannot find fails. The layout's stylesheet parse in `row-dialog.spec.js` and `nav-drawer.spec.js` also fails when any stylesheet link but the per-page one stops parsing, whatever its query string, attributes or quotes, not only the two whose order it is about (#276's review). **Textareas.** The FAQ questions (2 rows) and answers (4), and the asset text, advance reason and penalty reason (3, in the add form and the row window) are textareas, as legacy's are (`faqs/page.php:200-203`, `assets/page.php:207`, `advances/page.php:261`, `penalties/page.php:242`), and a test checks each one in both windows. **Option labels.** The FAQ and banner platform selects, the banner action select, the two list badges and the banner list's action cell show `platform_*` and `action_*` in legacy's option order, where they showed the stored value; `ContentOptionLabelsTest` checks every constant's key in both catalogues, and the banner and FAQ end-to-end tests read the labels and their order off the rendered pages. **Divergences.** Legacy's company reject form has no × (`companies/page.php:277-293`); the port's reject window keeps the one every row window has. Legacy's four FAQ windows put Save in no `.form-footer` (`faqs/page.php:164`, `:181`, `:214`, `:247`); the port's do, which keeps Save in reach while a long form scrolls. Legacy marks required fields with " *"; these windows and the row windows mark none, and their fields carry `required` (the setting-template windows keep legacy's markers). Legacy's FAQ, phone-country, guide-video and setting-template labels name no control; the port's name theirs, the setting-template windows' now included. **Still open, in #218's audit:** the banner form's action-dependent rows, WhatsApp country select, status select and image preview, and the notification form's audiences, company select, employee picker and script. |
| Related | **#214** (item 7), D-198, D-197, #270, #276, #218. |

## D-260: A List Toolbar's Filters Narrow Each Other, As Legacy's Do

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | Proposed 2026-09-17 in the pull request for #214 item 3 (its cascades; the phone scripts follow separately); accepted when the repository owner merges it. |
| Decision | The layout loads `org-filter-cascade.js`, as legacy's `layout.php:127` does on every page, and the requests page loads `request-filter-cascade.js`, as `requests/page.php:61` does. Both are the identical copies that sat unused in `_assets`. The toolbars of attendance, departments, employees and job titles carry what `org_filter_cascade_form_attrs()` writes (`org_helper.php:450-466`): `data-org-filters`, branches by company, departments by company and by branch, and job titles by department as JSON, the "All" and hint labels, and the filtered branch, department and job title to keep. Their branch, department and job title selects carry the markers the script finds them by, as legacy's do (`payroll_list_helper.php:77,88`, `departments/page.php:122`, `job_titles/page.php:105`, `employees/page.php:271,282,293`). The requests toolbar carries `hr_request_filter_form_attrs()`'s active request types by company (`hr_list_helper.php:970-979`), and its type select is rendered as `hr_render_request_type_filter_field()` renders it (`:981-999`): with no company chosen, disabled and asking for one. The org maps come from `AdminViewModelAdvice.orgFilterCascade()`, a supplier the toolbar reads once per request and only when it renders, D-252's pattern, over `OrgCascadeStore`. |
| Why | #214 item 3. The toolbars filtered but did not narrow. Changing the company left the branch, department and job title selects listing the previous company's rows, or every company's, until the form was submitted. A branch left the department select listing departments not linked to it, so a combination could filter the list to nothing, with nothing on the toolbar to say why. |
| Scope | **Every company's rows, for an administrator, whether or not the list is filtered.** The company select changes the other selects without a request, and every company is that session's reach. Legacy sends the same maps to every session, including one bound to a company: R-051 measured 3,671 rows across 283 companies. Here a session bound to one company gets nothing attached. No such session reaches these pages yet; when owner and HR logins arrive, the one supplier decides for all five toolbars. `OrgCascadeStore` lists a department under a branch, and a job title under a department, only within one company (R-051). The payload an administrator's page carries is no larger than legacy's for the same pages. This change adds five queries to each of the four pages' rendering, and one to the requests page's when it is filtered to a company; unfiltered, the grouped query replaces the one the type select used to run. |
| Divergences from legacy | **A session bound to one company.** Legacy attaches `org-filter-cascade.js` there too. With no company select to read, the script empties the branch, department and job title selects to "All" (`renderBranches` with no company), and `request-filter-cascade.js` throws on the missing select. The port attaches neither, and the server's lists stay. **Attendance** draws one toolbar, where legacy draws two, for the attendance list and its aggregate (`attendance/page.php:166,219`). |
| Also fixed | **The request type filter with no company.** The port listed each active type name once, under its lowest id (`MIN(id)` across companies). Choosing one filtered the list to the one company that owned that id, and "Annual" showed only one company's annual leave. Now, as in legacy, the select asks for a company first, and `EmployeeRequestStore.typeOptions` returns nothing without one. |
| Tests changed | Two assertions that no other company's name appears on a page are scoped past the toolbar's start tag, which D-260 deliberately fills with every company's rows for an administrator; each also asserts the tag does carry them, so the exception stays visible. |
| Not in this change | The toolbars' field order and labels, which still differ from legacy's on some of these pages (employees' status sits before its dates, and attendance's search comes first); those belong to the page-group issues under #211. `phone-validator.js` and `phone-form-bind.js`, the rest of #214 item 3: their forms need legacy's country-code select first. |
| Regression coverage | In the browser, with no stack (`deploy/e2e/tests/org-filter-cascade.spec.js`), the copied `org-filter-cascade.js` and `request-filter-cascade.js` run on toolbars shaped like the templates', with the maps written into attributes as JTE writes them. The spec checks that a filtered page lists the company's branches, the branch's departments and the department's job titles, keeping each choice. It also checks that changing the company, branch or department narrows the selects below it; that a branch with no departments shows the hint; that with every company the narrower selects wait for a company; the department-only and branch-only toolbars; and that a form without `data-org-filters` keeps the server's options. The request type select waits for a company, then lists that company's types and keeps the chosen one, and a name holding quotes and markup renders as text. The scripts themselves are unchanged copies, so the spec pins their behaviour on the attributes the templates now render. `AdminFilterCascadeTemplateTest` requires every toolbar select posting a branch, department or job title filter to carry its marker, and its form every attribute the script reads. It names the four toolbars it finds, and requires the layout to load the script; the request type filter is held the same way, with the requests page loading its script. `AdminLayoutWiringTest` checks the advice's supplier: every company's rows for an administrator, nothing for a session bound to one company, and read once and only when asked. `AdminEmployeesEndToEndTest` renders the employees toolbar filtered to one company. It checks that the four maps carry both companies' active rows exactly, with a retired branch left out, a department only under the branch it is linked to, and a name with quotes and `<` round-tripped; it also checks the kept filter values. `AdminRequestsEndToEndTest` checks the types map, with a retired type left out; the disabled select asking for a company; and a filtered select listing only that company's types, with the chosen one selected. Two existing tests asserted that another company's names appear nowhere on the page: `theFormOffersOnlyTheEditedEmployeesOwnCompanysOptions` and `theBranchFilterNarrowsToDepartmentsSpanningThatBranch`. The toolbar now carries those names for an administrator by decision, so each asserts that the toolbar's start tag carries them and that nothing else on the page does. With `main`'s templates, advice, controller and store, those six tests failed. Each mutant failed exactly the tests that pin it. The layout not loading the script failed the template gate and the employees toolbar test. Attendance's department select without its marker, and job titles' form without the pick-department hint, each failed the template gate. The cascade attached for a session bound to one company, and read on every call, each failed the wiring test; carrying one company's rows failed the wiring test and the employees toolbar test. The request type select not asking for a company, and retired types in the map, each failed the requests test. The requests page not loading its script failed the request gate and the requests test. Afterwards, on `main` with #266 and #271, 186 Java tests in 14 classes and all 86 stack-free browser tests passed. |
| Rollback | Revert the merge. Nothing is stored; every toolbar posts the same fields, except that with no company chosen the request type select is disabled and posts no `type_id`, as legacy's does. |
| Corrected 2026-09-17 (#273) | **Scope** said that "the one supplier decides for all five toolbars". Four did: attendance, departments, employees and job titles ask `AdminViewModelAdvice.orgFilterCascade()`, which reads the advice's session. The requests toolbar was decided in `AdminRequestsController` from the administrator view that controller builds for itself, so a session bound to one company, once one arrives through the advice, would still have been sent every company's request types. The controller now decides from the advice's session too, so that one session decides the maps all five toolbars attach; `AdminRequestsControllerTest` pins it. Whether a toolbar renders its company select is still decided from the administrator view each list controller builds in place of the advice's session, and owner and HR logins must change that too (recorded on #220, corrected under #270). The kept filter values were asserted only on the employees and requests toolbars; `AdminAttendanceEndToEndTest`, `AdminDepartmentsEndToEndTest` and `AdminJobTitlesEndToEndTest` now assert theirs. Both were found by #272's review. With `main`'s controller, exactly the controller test failed; each template keeping `0` for a filtered branch or department failed exactly its page's test. |
| Related | **#214** (item 3), R-051, D-252, D-250, D-249, #273. |

## D-261: The Company And Employee Forms Check A Phone As Legacy's Do

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | Proposed 2026-09-17 in the pull request for #214 item 3 (its phone scripts; the cascades were D-260); accepted when the repository owner merges it. |
| Decision | The company and employee forms take a phone the way legacy's do. **The country is a select of the active countries** (`phone_country_codes_for_select()`), each labelled flag, name in the page's language, then the code in brackets (`phone_country_option_label()`, `phone_countries_helper.php:375-397`). On the company form it is required and chooses `+20` for an add and the stored code for an edit (`_company_form.php:26-33`). On the employee form it comes before the phone and starts with an empty "Optional" choice (`_employee_form.php:93-103`). **Both forms carry `data-invalid-phone-msg`** (`companies/page.php:259,300`, `_employee_form.php:42`). **Their pages load legacy's number checks.** The layout renders `phone_countries_validation_rules_for_js()` (`:358-373`), then `phone-validator.js` and `phone-form-bind.js`. The phone then takes digits only, as many as the chosen country's numbers have; a number missing its leading zero gets it back on leaving the field; and a save whose number the country refuses is stopped with the form's message. The select and the rules come from one read of the active countries, `AdminViewModelAdvice.phoneCountries()`, a supplier read once per request and only when a form renders (D-252's pattern). The save's own check reads the same table, and, as legacy's does, judges `+20` by a fixed pattern rather than by its row. |
| Why | #214 item 3. The country code was a free text box, so a typo or a code no country has reached the server. The number itself was checked only after a round trip, and nothing kept it to digits or to the country's length while it was typed. |
| How the rules reach the page | Legacy's layout assigns `window.WorkinPhoneCountriesRules` in an inline script on every page. Here the JSON is the `data-rules` attribute of a script tag, `phone-countries-rules.js`, which assigns it. The template escapes it as an attribute, and the page keeps no inline script. The layout loads the rules and both scripts only when a page hands it rules, and only the company page with admin actions on and the employee page with its form open do, each reading the countries under the condition its form renders under. That is deliberate: `phone-form-bind.js` with no rules refuses every number, so the scripts never load without them. A page with no phone form reads no countries. |
| Divergences from legacy | **An employee edit keeps the phone and country code it was opened with.** D-229 checks an employee's phone and code on the server only when either is replaced, because stored rows hold pairs the rules refuse: `join_company.php` stores a phone with no code (R-019), and the development seed has 1,284 such rows. Legacy refuses those pairs both in the browser and in `employees/page.php:121-134`, so such an employee cannot be saved there until a country is chosen. Here the edit form carries `data-phone-keep-untouched`, and `phone-form-bind.js` lets a phone and code still as the form opened them through. Leaving the phone field rewrites it to digits with a restored leading zero, and a phone may be stored with a dial prefix or spaces, since `register_employee.php` stores it as typed; so a phone nobody typed in counts as opened while it normalizes to what it opened as, and the opened text is posted back, which the server keeps as stored instead of writing the rewrite as a new phone. A typed phone is judged, even the same number written in full, so an admin can still store a phone in its canonical form. That block is one of two changes to the copied script, and its comment says so. **A reopened company form syncs the phone's length.** Legacy opens its add form with a page load; the port's `crud.js` reopens it with `form.reset()`, which puts the country back without a change event, so the phone kept the last country's `maxlength` and refused a valid number. `phone-form-bind.js` syncs it once a reset has run; that is the other change. A changed phone or code is checked as legacy checks it. The company form is not marked, and it refuses an opened number its country refuses, as legacy's does; the company save checks it too. **A stored employee code no active country has** (its country retired) is listed and chosen, labelled with the code alone, as `phone_country_option_label()` labels an unknown code, so an unchanged save keeps it. Legacy's select drops it. **The scripts load only with a phone form**, not on every page; nothing else binds to them. |
| Not in this change | The employee form's layout around these fields: legacy draws country, phone and password in one "login credentials" grid with a hint (`_employee_form.php:90-117`), and the port keeps one field per row. Owner and HR settings forms that take a phone (`company_settings/_tab_users.php`, `profile/_edit_hr.php`), which have no port yet. |
| Operations | Two queries, `LegacyPhoneCountries`' table probe and its active countries, on each render of the company page with admin actions on and of the employee page with its form open. Nothing is stored or written differently: every form posts the same fields, and the country select posts a code the text box could have. |
| Regression coverage | In the browser, with no stack (`deploy/e2e/tests/phone-form.spec.js`), the page ends with `layout.jte`'s own phone block, read from the template and rendered with rules as JTE writes an attribute, and the scripts are served from the source tree. The spec checks that the rules reach the validator through the escaped attribute; that the company phone takes digits only, as many as the chosen country's numbers have; that a number without its leading zero gets it back on leaving the field; and that a number the country refuses stops the save with the form's message and focus on the phone, while a valid one saves. A company edit opened with a number its country refuses is refused. An employee needs no phone, but a phone needs a country. An employee edit saves the pair it was opened with, both a phone with no code and a code no country has; left through its phone field, it still saves a phone stored with a dial prefix, with spaces or without its zero, posting the stored text; a phone retyped as the same number in full saves what was typed; and it still checks a changed phone or a changed country; a company form reopened through `crud.js` after another country was chosen takes its own country's numbers again; an unmarked add refuses a phone with no country however it was opened. `AdminPhoneFormTemplateTest` finds every form with a phone and a `country_code`, names the two it finds, and requires each to draw a select, carry the message, hand the layout the rules, and read the countries under the `@if` its form renders under; it also requires the layout to load the three scripts only with rules, rules first, and nowhere else. `PhoneCountryChoicesTest` checks the labels in both languages, the Arabic fallback for a blank name, the rules' JSON with JSON and delimited prefixes, a blank code left out, and an empty rule set with no countries. `AdminLayoutWiringTest` checks the advice's supplier: labelled in the page's language, read once and only when asked, and no rules without the legacy database. `PlatformAdminFullFlowTest` renders the company form: required, `+20` chosen on an add and the stored code on an edit in English, a retired country left out, the message, and the rules and scripts in order; a page with no phone form loads none. `AdminEmployeesEndToEndTest` renders the employee form: "Optional" first and nothing chosen on an add, an active country labelled, a retired one left out, the message, the edit alone marked, the stored country chosen, and no phone script on the list without its form. It also saves unchanged an employee whose code no active country has. With `main`'s templates and advice and without `PhoneCountryChoices`, the five new Java tests that can run there failed (the unit and wiring tests need the new class to compile); one of them, the unchanged save, fails there only on its first assertion, because `main` draws a text box that already keeps the code. With `main`'s layout and `phone-form-bind.js` and no rules script, all nine browser tests of the first round failed; the three the review rounds added fail there too, because the spec renders the layout's phone block and `main` has none (corrected in #273). Each mutant failed only tests that pin it. Legacy's own `phone-form-bind.js` failed exactly the opened-pair test; an opened pair judged by its phone alone failed exactly the changed-pair test; every form keeping an opened pair, marked or not, failed exactly the company edit and the unmarked add; the rules script reading the wrong attribute failed the five tests that need a rule. The layout loading the scripts without rules, and the rules loading after the bind, each failed the layout gate and both form tests. Reading the countries on every call failed exactly the wiring test. Labels ignoring the language failed the label unit test, the wiring test and the company form test. A blank code becoming a rule failed exactly its unit test. An add choosing no country failed exactly the company form test, and the company form without its message failed the form gate and that test. The employee select dropping a stored code no active country has failed the new unchanged save and two existing unchanged-save tests, whose employees hold codes the test database has no country for. The employee edit not marked failed exactly the employee form test; the employees page handing the layout no rules failed the form gate and that test; and the list reading the countries without its form failed exactly that test. The first review round found that leaving the phone field broke the opened pair, and that the company page read the countries with admin actions off. With that round's `phone-form-bind.js`, exactly the left-through test failed, and so did posting the rewrite instead of the stored text. With that round's `companies.jte`, exactly the form gate failed, and so did reading the countries under a condition that does not wrap the form. The second round found that a reopened company form kept the last country's length, and that a retyped phone was put back. With that round's `phone-form-bind.js`, exactly the reopened-form and retyped-phone tests failed; a reset that does not sync the length failed exactly the first, and putting back a typed phone exactly the second. Afterwards, on `main` with #272, 126 Java tests in 14 classes passed (the phone, layout, stylesheet, message-key, spec-inventory, cascade, clock and asset gates, and the employees, full-flow, banners, active-checkbox and MySQL admin end-to-end classes), and all 98 stack-free browser tests passed three runs in a row. |
| Rollback | Revert the merge. Nothing is stored, and the server's checks are unchanged. |
| Related | **#214** (item 3), D-229, D-260, D-252, R-019. |

## D-262: The Employee Detail Page Draws Legacy's Layout, Badges And Figures

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | Proposed 2026-09-17 in the pull request for #261, which also closes #216's employee detail findings; accepted when the repository owner merges it. |
| Decision | `employee-detail.jte` renders `employees/detail.php` as legacy lays it out. **The header** is legacy's card: the photo, or an initials circle, beside the name, its yes/no badge and a bulleted list of the code, the stored phone, company, branch, department and hire date (`:52-70`), and the page title is "Employee — name" (`:37`). A blank name is an em dash in all three, as `dashboard_employee_display_name()` gives it (`:36`). **The four tables** sit two across (`:82-113`). **Attendance** has legacy's columns, date, check in, check out, hours and method, with the times to the minute, a yellow "still working" badge in the check-out cell of an open shift, and a dash for its hours (`:85-87`). **Requests and advances** draw their status as `badge()`, and **penalties** read type, days in red, date, and a yes/no badge for applied to payroll (`:95`, `:101-102`, `:109`). **Amounts** are `number_format(..., 0)` through `PayrollDisplay.money()`: the advances' amount and remaining, with remaining red while any is owed, the two money stat cards, and the payslip (`:77-78`, `:109`, `:118-127`). **The payslip** has legacy's seven figures: overtime green, penalties, medical insurance and advance deduction red, and the net salary large and blue with legacy's literal " ج.م". The medical insurance line shows `advances_deduction`, as legacy's does (`:124`). **Documents** are chips linking each file in a new tab (`:132-138`). **The hours card** prints the sum as PHP echoes a float, so eight hours read `8`. |
| Why | #261 and #216's employee detail audit. The page printed raw statuses (`approved`, `pending`), "Active"/"Inactive" for a yes/no flag, full datetimes, decimals without grouping (`5180.00`), six of the payslip's seven figures, and documents with no link to their files. |
| Divergences from legacy | **The photo's fallback.** Legacy swaps a photo that fails to load for a ui-avatars.com image; the port draws the initials circle locally (`img-fallback.js`), as its lists do, so no viewer's address reaches a third party. **A document link** is written only for an http or https URL, or one with no scheme. The upload endpoint stores its own absolute URL (`uploadFile()`), so this refuses nothing it wrote, and a `javascript:` value written some other way shows as a chip without a link. **Phone widths.** Legacy keeps the four tables two across at every width; below 768px, app-responsive.css's tablet breakpoint, they stack. **Styles.** Legacy writes the layout in style attributes; the port's `emp-detail-*` classes in `admin-extra.css` carry what those attributes compute to. That includes the card's larger radius and shadow, which app-ui.css gives legacy's card through `.content > div[style*="border-radius:12px"]`, a selector no class matches. `employee-detail.spec.js` checks it. **The title escapes the name once.** Legacy escapes the name into `$pageTitle` and `layout.php` escapes the title again, so a name like `O'Neil` reads `O&#039;Neil` in its title and heading; the port's reads `O'Neil`. |
| Also changed | `EmployeeDisplay.initials()` is `dashboard_avatar_initials_label()` (`includes/media.php:106-125`): the letters are upper-cased, where the port kept their case. Its own blank case is `?`, which no legacy page reaches: each substitutes a name first, and so does the port. The detail page uses an em dash, the employees list's avatar `E` (`employee_helper.php:506`), and the companies list's `C` (`company_helper.php:173`, `trim($name) ?: 'C'`, so `"0"` too). The port's lists wrote `؟`, and the detail page drew no initials. |
| Not in this change | The lists write legacy's initials as one span per letter (`dashboard_avatar_initials_html()`, `includes/employee_helper.php:508`); the port's lists keep one text node. The list pages' name cells still print a blank name empty where legacy prints an em dash (#279). |
| Regression coverage | `EmployeeDetailTest`: the hours card as PHP echoes a float, the attendance times and dash, whole-pound advances and their colour, which document URLs are linked, the initials, and a blank name's fallback. `employee-detail.spec.js` (browser project) draws the page twice under its stylesheets, once with the classes and once with legacy's style attributes, each element where the template puts it. At 1440 and 1024px it fails on any computed property of any marked element that differs, and it fails on a class with no pair. `AdminEmployeesEndToEndTest` and `PlatformAdminFullFlowTest` render an employee and a company with no name and read their avatars. `AdminEmployeeDetailEndToEndTest` reads the rendered page against a real database: the header, title, avatar, a blank name, photo fallback, raw phone and dash for no hire date; the attendance columns and times; the request, penalty and advance badges, figures and colours; the seven payslip figures and currency; and the document links. `AdminTableConventionsTest` expects the page's two yes/no badges. |
| Rollback | Revert the merge. Nothing is stored or queried differently. |
| Corrected 2026-09-20 (#215) | **The scheme check is now `StoredUrl`, and it refuses one more thing.** The rule moved out of `EmployeeDetail.Document` so the company detail page and the companies list share it, and it now also refuses a value that opens with two separators in any combination (`//host`, `\\host`, `/\host`, `\/host`), and any value carrying a control character. Two separators name another origin while naming no scheme, so the branch that treats a schemeless value as a path on this host must not pass it through; a browser reads a backslash as a slash there, so a prefix test on `//` alone was stepped around by the other three forms and by `/<tab>/host` (#292's review round 2 read five such links out of the running page). The control-character refusal is wider than that and rests on a different reason: a browser drops tab, newline, carriage return and a leading control before parsing, so the text checked would not be the address followed, and the rest -- `U+007F` and an interior control, which a browser keeps and percent-encodes -- are refused because no value this system writes carries one. D-264 records the same-host divergence that creates. A document URL stored that way is shown as an unlinked chip, as one with another scheme already was. |
| Related | **#261**, **#216** (employee detail), #214 (items 5 and 6), D-255, R-057. |

## D-263: Dashboard Request Numbers Are Read With PHP's `(int)` Cast, And Page Offsets Are Long

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | Proposed 2026-09-17 in the pull request for #249; accepted when the repository owner merges it. |
| Decision | Every hand-written helper in the dashboard that stands in for legacy's `(int)` cast of a request value now reads it with `PhpCast.intval`, PHP 8's cast, which `PhpCastTest` holds to PHP 8.3.33's own answers (D-249). The cast reads the leading decimal or exponent number, so `"1e2"` is 100, `"1.9e1"` is 19, `"5abc"` is 5 and `"abc"` is 0. **Where it applies:** the list filters' page, page size and ids (`DashboardListFilters`, `CompanyListFilters`), the company filter (`DashboardOrgScope`), a branch's radius and a department's branch ids (`Branch`, `Department`), payroll's run, row id, month and year, activities' page and page size, requests' type, leave balances' year, the employee detail page's id, month and year, attendance's aggregate page, the employees page's filter and form ids, an employee's contract duration, a company's activity, title and size, the sort order, phone length and category of guide videos, phone countries, FAQs and banners, and the sort order of the settings page's definitions and options. Each helper keeps its own rule for an absent or blank value. **Bounds.** A value bound for an `int` field or column is bounded to the `int` range with `Math.clamp`, where PHP's 64-bit value would reach legacy's insert or query. The settings page's sort orders had a narrowing cast instead, which wrapped 3000000000 to a negative order; they are bounded too. An id is not bounded: the employee detail page keeps its id's 64-bit value, so an id past the `int` range names no employee, as in legacy, rather than opening employee 2147483647. **Offsets.** A page number can now reach `Integer.MAX_VALUE`, and its offset does not fit an `int`, so `DashboardPage.offsetFor`, its `from` and `to`, and the activities page's offset are `long`. **Gate.** `AdminPhpIntCastTest` fails on any `Integer.parseInt`, `Long.parseLong`, `valueOf`, `decode` or `new BigInteger` in `platformadmin`; a digit loop written by hand is not caught. Its one allowed use, `AdminDeviceView.id`, prints an id the database returned. |
| Why | #249, from #248's review. The helpers kept only a number's leading digits, reading `"1e2"` as 1, or used Java's parse, refusing `"5abc"` and `"1e2"` and falling back to 0 or a default. **The offset was already wrong on `main`:** `?page=2147483647` on a list gave `(page - 1) * perPage` wrapped negative, and the database refused the negative `OFFSET`. The activities page masked it with `max(0, offset)` and showed page 1's rows. |
| Divergences from legacy | **Bounds.** Legacy's page number and size, sort orders, phone length and contract months are PHP's 64-bit integers. A sort order or contract past 2147483647 fails legacy's insert against its `int` column; the port stores the bound. A phone length that large is refused on both sides by the 4 to 15 check before any insert (corrected 2026-09-19 in #259's change, from #284's review round 2). A page past that bound is `Integer.MAX_VALUE`, which lists nothing, as legacy's page does. **A blank or out-of-range year or month.** These predate this change and are now recorded. Leave balances read a blank, unreadable or non-positive `year` as this year. Legacy's cast gives 0 for a blank or unreadable year, or the number itself for a negative one. Its list then shows that year's balances, which is none, and a crafted add with such a year writes it. The employee detail page reads a blank `month` or `year` as this month or year, and a month outside 1 to 12 as this month, where legacy's cast gives 0 or the raw month, which selects no attendance, payslip or leave. |
| Not in this change | The `(float)` casts, which stop at the decimal digits in the same way (#280). Numbers bound by Spring as numeric `@RequestParam`s, which answer 400 where legacy's cast reads 0: ids, and payroll's posted month and year (#281). |
| Regression coverage | Unit: `DashboardListFiltersTest`, `CompanyListFiltersTest`, `OrgFormCastTest`, `DashboardOrgScopeTest` (exponents, and a 23-digit id saturating to `Long.MAX_VALUE` as PHP's does, where the test had expected it cleared), `DashboardPageTest` (the last page's offset and range), `CompanyFormTest`, `GuideVideoFormTest`, `PhoneCountryFormTest`, `FaqFormTest`, `BannerFormTest` and `EmployeeContractMonthsTest` (exponents, trailing text, and the `int` bound for months and years). End to end: `AdminPayrollEndToEndTest` (`run_id=<id>e0`), `AdminBranchesEndToEndTest` (`?page=2147483647` and `1e10`), `AdminActivitiesEndToEndTest` (`per_page=2e1`), `AdminRequestsEndToEndTest` (`type_id=<id>e0`), `AdminLeaveBalancesEndToEndTest` (`year=2.022e3`), `AdminEmployeeDetailEndToEndTest` (`id=<id>e0&month=3e0&year=2.026e3`, and an id past the `int` range beside a stored employee 2147483647), `AdminSettingsEndToEndTest` (sort orders past the `int` range), `AdminAttendanceEndToEndTest` (`agg_page=2e0`), `AdminEmployeesEndToEndTest` (`filter_job_title=<id>e0`) and `AdminWorkforcePlanningEndToEndTest` (D-249's correction). `AdminPhpIntCastTest` is the gate. **Evidence.** Each site was put back to `main`'s code on its own, with the new tests, and every file restored byte-identical after each run. Exactly the named tests failed, in 20 cases: each of the eighteen files holding the nineteen helpers (with the guide video form's `Integer.parseInt`, the source gate failed too), `WorkforcePlan` and its store's `getInt` (the list answered 500), and `DashboardPage`'s `int` offsets, with the activities controller, store and template that pass it `int`s (`DashboardPageTest`, and `?page=2147483647` on branches). One mutant, the gate's allowed parse replaced, failed exactly `everyAllowedParseIsStillThere`. `OrgFormCastTest`'s branch ids test first passed on `main`'s leading-digits parse, because none of its inputs had an exponent; it now reads `"1e1"`, and fails there. |
| Rollback | Revert the merge. Nothing is stored differently, except that a value typed with an exponent or trailing text is now stored as PHP reads it. |
| Related | **#249**, #248, D-249, #280, #281. |

## D-264: The Company Detail Page Shows Legacy's Card, Counts And Tables

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | Proposed 2026-09-19 in the pull request for #215's company detail findings; accepted when the repository owner merges it. |
| Decision | `company-detail.jte` renders `companies/detail.php` as legacy lays it out. **The title** is "company — name" (`:29`). **The quick links** are back, then this company's branches, employees and payroll, each with `?company_id=`, which sets the dashboard's company filter as legacy's links do (`:33-38`). **The header card** holds the logo in legacy's 72px box, the name with its status badge, the stored phone, the email or a dash, the OTP flag as a yes/no badge, the registration date, and the commercial registration button when one is stored (`:40-52`). **Six counts**, in legacy's order and colours: active employees (labelled `total_employees`, legacy's label), all employees, branches, employees checked in today, pending requests and pending advances (`:54-61`). **Three tables** (`:63-84`).
