Every branch, active or not, by name, with its active employees, headed by the count and an edit link to the branches page. The HR, manager and company-admin employees' phones and role badges, in the role enum's order. The first 15 employees, active first and then by name, with #, the code (else the id), the name (else a dash), phone, branch (else a dash), hire date (else a dash), a yes/no badge and a Details link to `/admin/employee_detail?id=`, headed by the total and an "all" link, and from the sixteenth legacy's "و N موظف — الكل" row. An empty table has no row, in legacy and here. `PlatformAdminCompanyDirectory.CompanyDetail` carries the card's fields (`Profile`), the four new counts and the three lists, and `LegacyPlatformAdminCompanyDirectory.detail()` reads them. |
| Why | #215's company_detail audit, and the repository owner's comparison of 2026-09-14. The port showed the name, a back link, the id, the status and two counts, and none of legacy's card, links or tables. |
| Queries | `detail.php:11-27`'s queries, parameterized and scoped to the one company as legacy scopes them. They are the company row; `COUNT(*)` of its active employees and of all of them; `COUNT(DISTINCT employee_id)` of attendance joined to its employees where `DATE(check_in) = CURDATE()`, in the zone the legacy connection sets (D-099); the two pending counts through `employees`, as before; its branches, with a correlated count of each branch's active employees; its HR users; and its employees joined to their branch. **Two differences.** The employees table reads 15 rows with `LIMIT` rather than every row, and its count is the total already counted. Each ordering ends on the id (`b.name, b.id`; `role, id`; `is_active DESC, first_name, last_name, id`), so rows that tie on legacy's keys come in one order; legacy's come as the server returns them. `rowsThatTieOnLegacysKeysComeOutByTheirId` seeds a tie in each of the three tables and reads the order; it pins the orderings as a whole and cannot prove the tie-break alone, because a server may return ties in that order without being asked to. The page ran four queries and now runs nine, each filtered or joined on columns legacy's schema indexes (`fk_employee_company`, `fk_employee_branch`, `fk_branch_company`, `index_employee_date`, `fk_request_employee`, `fk_advance_employee`); no plan was measured. Nothing is written. |
| Kept | The port's own parts stay: the route `/admin/companies/{id}` and its access, the rejection reason, the outstanding-work notice, the approve, reject, suspend and restore buttons behind the actions switch with their audit rows, and the reject dialog. They sit between the counts and the tables. Edit and the typed-name delete stay in the list's row menu; legacy's detail page has neither. |
| Divergences from legacy | **The logo's fallback.** Where no logo is stored, or its file is gone, `company_logo_src()` draws a ui-avatars.com image. The port draws the initials locally in the logo's box, as the list does (`img-fallback.js`), so that fallback reaches no third party. **The logo's address.** `company_logo_src()` reaches `dashboard_media_url()` only for a value that names http or https, or that is a file on this server (`company_media_file_exists()`, `company_helper.php:146-176`), and draws the avatar otherwise, so a stored `//host/p.png` never becomes a request. The port has no file check and read the column straight into the `src` on this page and on the list; both now go through `StoredUrl`, and a value it refuses draws the initials. A stored `https://` logo is still loaded, as legacy loads it. **The commercial registration button** links only an http, https or schemeless URL, D-262's rule, and carries `rel="noopener"`. Legacy links the stored value as it is. **Phone widths.** Legacy keeps the branch and HR tables two across at every width; below 768px they stack, as the employee detail's do. **Styles.** Legacy's style attributes are `company-detail-*` classes in `admin-extra.css`, carrying what those attributes compute to, including the larger radius and shadow app-ui.css gives legacy's card. The card, the stats' margin and the two-across grid share the employee detail's rules. **Title escaping.** Legacy escapes the name twice in its title, as D-262 records for the employee detail; the port escapes it once. **A company with no name** has a blank title and card name, as legacy's does. The port's "unnamed company" label is gone from this page; the delete page keeps it. **A registration URL that is not a web address.** Legacy's detail page gates its button on PHP truthiness and legacy's list draws the anchor whatever the value is, because `dashboard_media_url()` prefixes anything but http and https with legacy's own host, giving a dead same-host link. The port draws no anchor at all in that case, and treats a stored `0` as no value on both pages, as `detail.php:50` and `page.php:218` do. `StoredUrl` also refuses a value opening with two separators, whichever way each leans: that names another origin without naming a scheme, and the schemeless branch must not pass it through as a path on this host. It refuses any character below U+0020, and U+007F, for a different reason: a browser drops some of them before parsing (tab, newline and carriage return anywhere, and a leading control), so the text checked would not be the address followed, and the rest are refused because no value this system writes carries one. That refusal is wider than the disagreement and diverges from legacy on this host too: legacy links `/uploads/a<newline>b.pdf` and the browser fetches `/uploads/ab.pdf` from this server, where the port draws no link and no image at all. |
| Also changed | **`StoredUrl.href()`** is D-262's scheme check, moved out of `EmployeeDetail.Document` so the company pages use it too. **The companies list's commercial registration link** goes through it, where the port linked the stored value as it is. Legacy's list never links another scheme either: `dashboard_media_url()` prefixes anything that is not http or https with its own host (`includes/media.php:84-102`). **The card's and the list's logo** read the same column through `Profile.logoSrc()` and `CompanyRow.logoSrc()`, so `hasLogo()` now means "a logo this page may load" rather than "a value is stored". **The employee detail's stacked tables** now scroll inside their `.table-wrap` below 768px. A bare `1fr` column took the width of the widest table, whose headers do not wrap, so the tables ran past the edge of the screen and could not be read there. The column is `minmax(0, 1fr)` on both detail pages. `CompanyRow.avatarName(String)` is shared with the detail page. `AdminTableConventionsTest` expects this page's two yes/no badges. |
| Not in this change | Company and HR sessions: legacy's `isCompany()` branch sends an owner to their own company, and it has no counterpart because the port's dashboard signs in the administrator alone. **The other stored images.** An employee's photo (`employee-detail.jte:64`, `employees.jte:445`) and a banner's image (`banners.jte:87`, `home.jte:72`) still reach an `<img src>` without this rule; **#295** tracks them, each to ride the next change to its page, because `employees.jte` is being changed for #216 and the banner pages belong to #218. |
| Regression coverage | `PlatformAdminFullFlowTest` renders the page against a real MariaDB beside a second company that has a branch, an HR employee, a check-in today, and a pending request and advance. `theCompanyDetailPageShowsLegacysCardCountsAndTablesForThatCompanyAlone` reads the title in Arabic and English, the four links, the card (logo, name and badge, phone, email, OTP, date, registration), the six counts in order and colour, and the three tables row by row as exact markup: the branches by name, one of them inactive, with their active employees; the staff in the enum's order with their role badges; and the employees active first, with a blank code shown as the id and a missing hire date as a dash. The counts are chosen to catch a wrong filter: 3 of 4 employees active, 2 employees checked in today from three check-ins today and one yesterday, 1 pending request of 2, and 2 pending advances of 3. None of the other company's rows, phones or links appear. `theEmployeesTableListsFifteenAndCountsTheRestFromTheSixteenth` renders fifteen employees with no "more" row, then adds an inactive one that sorts first by name, and reads the same fifteen rows and "و 1 موظف — الكل". `aCompanyWithNothingUnderItShowsLegacysBlanksAndEmptyTables` reads a pending signup with no name, email or logo: the blank title, the "C" initials, a dash for the email, "no" for OTP, six zeros, three empty tables, and the approve and reject buttons. `aCommercialRegistrationIsLinkedOnlyWhenItIsAWebAddress` stores `javascript:` registrations (plain, mixed case after a space, after a control character, and with a tab or a newline in the scheme) and a `data:` one, and finds no link on the detail page or the list; an https one is linked on both. `StoredUrlTest`, `CompanyRowTest` and `CompanyDetailTest` check the link rule and the formatting. `company-detail.spec.js` (browser project) draws each classed element twice under the page's stylesheets, with the class and with legacy's attribute, and compares every computed property at 1440 and 1024px. It compares the initials' box with legacy's logo box, and at 390px it checks that the tables stack and a wide one scrolls in its own wrap; a new test in `employee-detail.spec.js` checks the same for that page. `AdminTableConventionsTest` expects the page's two yes/no badges. **Evidence** (`companydetail/evidence.json`, eleven cases, each exact: the six first written, the two round 1 added for a protocol-relative link and a stored `0`, the two round 2 added for the two halves of the separator-and-control-character rule, and the one round 3 added for the logo, which loads the stored value outside the rule.) With `main`'s two templates, directory, store, `CompanyRow` and `EmployeeDetail`, and no `StoredUrl`, exactly the four new end-to-end tests and the badge gate failed; `CompanyDetailTest` and `StoredUrlTest` were removed and `CompanyRowTest` put back to `main`'s for that run, because they cannot compile against it. With `main`'s `admin-extra.css`, exactly the two computed-style comparisons, the two box checks, the class count and the employee detail's phone test failed; the company page's phone test passes there, because with no class its tables are plain blocks. Dropping the active-first order failed exactly the page test and the fifteen test. Showing the "more" row from the fifteenth employee failed exactly the fifteen test and its unit test. Linking a stored URL whatever its scheme failed exactly the six tests that pin the rule: the company end-to-end test, `StoredUrlTest`, `CompanyRowTest`, `CompanyDetailTest`, and the employee detail's unit and end-to-end document tests. A bare `1fr` stacked column failed exactly the two phone tests. Every case runs the harness's seven Java classes, and the two browser cases its two specs; the counts each run measured are in `evidence.json` rather than repeated here, because a figure written once ages at every round. At this head those seven hold 70 tests and all pass: `PlatformAdminFullFlowTest` 24, `AdminEmployeeDetailEndToEndTest` 21, `AdminTableConventionsTest` 10, `EmployeeDetailTest` 6, `StoredUrlTest` 4, `CompanyDetailTest` 3, `CompanyRowTest` 2; the two specs hold 10, and the whole stack-free browser project passed three runs in a row when the styles were written. The review rounds added four of those tests: `rowsThatTieOnLegacysKeysComeOutByTheirId` (round 1), `StoredUrlTest`'s two-separator and control-character tests (round 2, whose values that reviewer supplied), and `aStoredLogoIsLoadedOnlyWhenItStaysOnThisHost` (round 3), which stores five off-host logos and a `javascript:` one on the detail page and the list and finds the initials drawn instead. |
| Rollback | Revert the merge. Nothing is stored or written differently. |
| Related | **#215** (company_detail), #211, D-262, D-163, D-099, ADR-0016. |

## D-265: A Blank Employee Name Reads As Legacy's Dash Wherever Legacy Prints It Through Its Helper

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | Proposed 2026-09-19 in the pull request for #279; accepted when the repository owner merges it. |
| Decision | Where legacy prints an employee's name through `dashboard_employee_display_name()` (`includes/employee_helper.php:130-152`), the port prints `EmployeeDisplay.displayName(name, "—")`, so an employee whose first and last names are both blank reads as an em dash rather than an empty cell. **Name cells:** the employees list (`employees/page.php:343`), requests (`requests/page.php:122`), and every table legacy draws with `hr_render_table_employee_cells()` (`hr_list_helper.php:66-73`): advances (`advances/page.php:208`), penalties (`penalties/page.php:179`), assets (`assets/page.php:164`), leave balances (`leave_balances/page.php:114`), attendance's punch table (`attendance/page.php:201`) and a payroll run's payslips (`payroll/page.php:281`). **Row actions:** legacy builds each row action's employee from the same helper (`hr_requests_row_actions()` `hr_list_helper.php:524`, `hr_leave_balance_row_actions()` `:614`, `hr_penalties_row_actions()` `:660`, `hr_assets_row_actions()` `:718`, `hr_advances_row_actions()` `:779`, `payroll_attendance_row_actions()` `payroll_list_helper.php:494`), so the port's subject line on each row window takes the dash, and so does the label an edit's picker falls back to when the row's employee is not in its list, keeping the code as legacy's does (`— (CODE)`). **The employees edit window** is titled as `employees/page.php:399` titles it, "Edit employee: name" (`edit_employee`, already in both catalogues), where the port wrote only "Edit". Its row is `SELECT e.*`, so the helper reads the two stored names: `Employee.Form.displayName()` trims each, joins the pair, trims it, and gives the dash for a blank pair. |
| Why | #279, from #278's review. The stores select the name as legacy's SQL does (`TRIM(CONCAT(COALESCE(first_name,''), ' ', COALESCE(last_name,'')))`), which is empty for an employee stored with no name, for example by an import, and the port printed that empty string where legacy's helper substitutes the dash. #278 fixed the detail page and the list avatars; this change covers the list pages' name cells and row actions, and the employees edit window's title. |
| What counts as blank | On a list row the helper returns `trim($row['employee_name'])` unless that is empty, then tries the first and last names (not selected on a list row), then a `name` column (not in this schema), then the fallback. SQL's `TRIM` strips spaces only, so a name that is only a tab survives the query and PHP's `trim` empties it: `displayName()`'s `isBlank()` treats it as blank too. |
| Left as legacy prints them | **Attendance's aggregate report** prints the name its SQL returns (`attendance/page.php:242`, `payroll_list_helper.php:473`), so a blank name stays blank there. **A payslip's edit window** is titled with the raw `employee_name` (`payroll/page.php:335`), so its name part stays blank. Both templates now say so beside the markup. **The employee pickers' options** are `hr_employee_option_label()` (`hr_helper.php:192-203`), which trims the SQL name and substitutes nothing; `EmployeePicker` keeps showing the code alone for a blank name, its recorded divergence from legacy's leading space. **Join requests** print `name ?: phone` (`join_requests/page.php:54`), as `JoinRequest.label()` does. **Complaints** print `complaints_submitter_label()` (`hr_list_helper.php:1288-1300`), a fallback chain of their own. **Device punches** have no legacy page (D-258). |
| Divergences from legacy | **A name that is exactly `0`.** The helper tests `!empty($row['employee_name'])`, and PHP's `empty("0")` is true, so on a list row an employee whose first name is `0` and last name blank reads `—` in legacy; the port prints `0`. The detail page and the edit title read a `SELECT e.*` row, where the helper's split-name branch returns `0`, and so does the port. The employees list's `E` avatar has had the same difference since D-262. **Whitespace outside PHP's `trim` set**, such as a form feed or U+3000, is blank to `isBlank()` and printed by legacy. |
| Also changed | D-244 gains a correction row: it said the Edit buttons on advances, assets and penalties label a blank-named row's employee by its code alone, and they now read "— (CODE)". `EmployeePicker.label()`'s Javadoc says the same. No store, query or message changes. |
| Not in this change | **Two places print a dash where legacy prints nothing.** The activity feed on the home and activities pages (`Activity.name()`): legacy's `home_present_activity()` substitutes `—` only for a NULL name (`home_service.php:1077`), and its SQL name is never NULL. A notification's recipient (`notifications.jte`): legacy prints `$n['to_name'] ?? '—'` (`notifications/page.php:196-198`) over the same never-NULL expression, joined with a LEFT JOIN (`helper.php:295`). Both predate this change. **The payslip edit window** joins "Edit" and the name with an em dash, where legacy writes a colon ("Edit: name"). **The company detail page's employee list** (`companies/detail.php:80`) prints through the helper and has no port yet; when it is ported it takes the same fallback. |
| Regression coverage | Each page's end-to-end test seeds an employee with blank first and last names beside a named one, renders the page against a real database, and reads the named row too, so a dash printed everywhere fails. `AdminEmployeesEndToEndTest`: the name cell reads `—`; the edit window reads "تعديل موظف: —" for a blank pair, "تعديل موظف: Aya" for a first name alone and "تعديل موظف: Aya Alpha" for a padded first name, and the add window keeps its own title. `AdminRequestsEndToEndTest`: the cell and both decision subjects, for a blank name and for a name that is only a tab. `AdminAdvancesEndToEndTest`, `AdminPenaltiesEndToEndTest` and `AdminAssetsEndToEndTest`: the cell, the edit's subject (and the advance's reject subject), and the picker's fallback label `— (A200)`. `AdminLeaveBalancesEndToEndTest`: the cell and the edit's subject. `AdminAttendanceEndToEndTest`: the punch table's cell and edit subject read `—`, and the aggregate report's cell stays empty. `AdminPayrollEndToEndTest`: a run's payslip row reads `—` before its code. With `main`'s eight templates and `Employee.java`, exactly the nine new tests failed, of 231 in the eight end-to-end classes and the four template gates. Each of four mutants failed exactly the tests that pin it: the aggregate report given the dash failed only the attendance test (29 run); the pickers' fallback label taking the raw name failed only the advances, penalties and assets tests (59 run); the edit title joining the stored names without trimming each failed only the title test (60 run); and `displayName()` testing `isEmpty()` rather than `isBlank()` failed only the requests test, on its tab-only name, and `EmployeeDetailTest`'s blank-name unit test (228 run, both employee detail classes among them). Every file was restored byte for byte and hash-checked after each run. Afterwards 258 tests in 15 classes passed: the eight end-to-end classes, both employee detail classes, `EmployeePickerTest`, and the stylesheet, message-key, layout-wiring and table-convention gates. |
| Rollback | Revert the merge. Nothing is stored or queried differently. |
| Corrected 2026-09-20 (#215) | **The company detail page's employee list** is ported in the same wave, in D-264, and reads `CompanyDetail.Employee.nameLabel()`, which is `EmployeeDisplay.displayName(name, "—")`. So it takes this fallback, as this entry said it would, and its end-to-end test pins the dash. |
| Related | **#279**, #278, D-262, #211, #216. |

## D-266: The Dashboard's Assets Are Cached, And Its Icons Are Small Copies Of The Logo

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | Proposed 2026-09-19 in the pull request for #259; accepted when the repository owner merges it. The owner chose it on 2026-09-19, answering "Both (Recommended)" to a seven-day cache for `/admin/_assets/**` and resized favicon copies. |
| Decision | `AdminAssetCaching` serves `/admin/_assets/**` itself, from the same classpath location. **Images** (`*.png`) are sent with `Cache-Control: max-age=604800`, seven days, and a content ETag. **Stylesheets, scripts and every other file** are sent with `Cache-Control: no-cache` and a content ETag. The browser revalidates each one on every load and gets a 304 with no body while its copy is current. The ETag is the SHA-256 of the file, computed once per file. Neither kind sends `Last-Modified` or honours `If-Modified-Since`. **Icons.** The layout's and sign-in page's favicon and touch icon are 32 and 180 pixel copies of legacy's `logo.png`: `favicon-32.png` (1,974 bytes) and `apple-touch-icon.png` (40,574 bytes), resized with Lanczos. The sidebar and the sign-in page's two images keep the original file. |
| Why | #259. On `main` every asset answered `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, must-revalidate`, Spring Security's default for a response that sets none, so a browser stored nothing and downloaded every stylesheet, script and image again on every page. #259 had assumed there was no header at all and the browser guessed. The 1,364,971-byte logo was the favicon of every page, and the sidebar's image. |
| Divergence from the owner's choice | The owner chose a seven-day cache for everything under `/admin/_assets/**`. Stylesheets and scripts are revalidated instead, because their URLs carry no version. A seven-day cache would keep a browser on a stylesheet from before a deploy for up to a week. The jar's timestamps cannot serve as the check either: Gradle 9 builds reproducible archives, so every entry carries the same fixed time. The cost is one conditional request per file per page, answered with a 304 and no body. Versioned URLs would allow a long cache for these too, but they touch every asset link in the templates and the fifteen tests and specs that match those links, so they are not in this change. |
| Divergences from legacy | Legacy's icons are the full logo (`includes/layout.php:150-151`, `pages/login/page.php:67-68`); the port's are copies. D-254 gains a correction row. Legacy's own asset caching is set by its web server, outside its repository, and is not copied. |
| Not in this change | Versioned asset URLs. The sidebar and the sign-in page still show the original logo, now cached for seven days after the first page. |
| Operations | On the wire, images carry `Cache-Control: max-age=604800`, and stylesheets and scripts carry `no-cache` with an `ETag`. A changed stylesheet shows on the next page load after a deploy. If a browser ever shows an old one, compare `curl -sI <host>/admin/_assets/style.css`'s `ETag` with the browser's cached copy. |
| Regression coverage | `PlatformAdminAssetsExposureTest`: `theIconsAreSmallCopiesOfTheLogo` reads each icon's PNG header for its size, and requires it under 64 KiB. `anImageIsCachedForSevenDaysAgainstAContentEtag`. `aStylesheetIsRevalidatedAgainstItsContentRatherThanItsTimestamp`: both require the ETag to be the SHA-256 of the body just downloaded; a matching ETag gets a 304; an old ETag gets the file even with a future `If-Modified-Since`; a script is `no-cache` too. `AdminLayoutWiringTest.theLayoutAndTheSignInPageCarryLegacysLogo` now pins the two icon links. **Evidence.** Six cases, each with every file restored byte-identical after its run. With `main`'s serving (no `AdminAssetCaching`), exactly the two caching tests fail, both reading `no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, must-revalidate`. With `main`'s templates and no icon copies, exactly the icon, image-cache and layout icon tests fail. Four mutants fail exactly the tests that pin them: stylesheets cached for seven days, stylesheets revalidated by their timestamp, no content ETag, and an ETag that hashes the resource's URL rather than its content. |
| Rollback | Revert the merge. The assets go back to the default serving. A browser holding a cached image keeps it for up to seven days, which is harmless. |
| Related | **#259**, D-254, #255. |

## D-267: An Org Write That Matches No Row Is Refused, Rather Than Flashing Success

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | Proposed 2026-09-20 in the pull request for #286; accepted when the repository owner merges it. |
| Decision | The six org writes that read neither the row nor the count now refuse a write whose update matches no row: the branch and shift `saveEdit`, and the delete on all four pages. Each throws `NO_ROW`, which the four controllers show as `no_data` ("No data found" / "لا توجد بيانات"), and no audit row is written. An unchanged save and a repeat delete stay a success, because the connection counts matched rows, not changed ones (D-253's #256 row, `LegacyRowCountStartupCheck`). |
| Why | #286, from #285's review round 1. An administrator's row ownership is checked on neither side (R-044), so for those six writes the update's count was the only thing that could catch a stale tab after a company's cascade delete, or a crafted id -- and nothing read it. The page flashed success and the audit log gained "branch updated in company N" for a row that does not exist. |
| The flash key | Legacy flashes `error_required` when its count is 0 (`branches/page.php:41-77`, `departments/page.php:62-71`, `job_titles/page.php:41-67`, `shifts/page.php:32-58`), which tells the operator a required field is missing when none is. This uses `no_data`, which legacy uses for a row that is not there (`companies/detail.php:12`, and the other detail pages). Recorded as a divergence in wording, not in outcome: both refuse. |
| Also changed | **D-253's "Corrected 2026-09-19 (#256)" row** said, in the present tense, that the org services ignore the count and flash success "whatever the connection counts". That was true until this change and is now the opposite of what the code does, so the row is corrected and points here. **`LegacyRowCountStartupCheck`'s Javadoc** listed the frozen-PHP stores that depend on matched-row counting; it now lists these six writes too, and says what an operator would see if the guard were relaxed: an administrator told `no_data` about a row in front of them. **`AdminTemplateMessageKeyTest`** gains a gate for the keys a controller hands the page: the template scanner sees only `t.apply(errorKey)`, so a key invented in a `messageKey` switch was checked by nothing. It reads the arms, returns and `case` labels -- wrapped over lines or not -- of every `messageKey`, `errorKey` and `messageFor` method, a key put into the model as `errorKey`, a key spelled into a redirect as `?error=`, and a key a controller translates itself with `apply("...")`, and resolves each in both catalogues. **It is a floor, not a census.** Every round of this pull request's review found a shape the scan could not read -- rounds 2 and 3 three each, round 4 three more, each proved with a mutant that left the suite green -- and three successive attempts to write down what remained were each falsified by the next shape found. So this row does not enumerate the remainder: it records that a source scan reads the shapes it knows and no others. **#296** carries the work of following a key to the page instead of matching its spelling, and **#294** the `device_error_` family, which is built rather than written and which no scan can reach. |
| Not in this change | The department and job title `saveEdit`, which already refuse a missing row with `error_db` through `ownerOf()`. The company writes, which already refuse anything but a count of 1. Legacy's own department `save_edit`, which ignores the count and then dies on the `department_branches` foreign key (D-253's #256 row). |
| Regression coverage | `aSaveOrDeleteForAnIdThatMatchesNoRowIsRefusedAndAuditsNothing` in `AdminBranchesEndToEndTest` and `AdminShiftsEndToEndTest`, and `aDeleteForAnIdThatMatchesNoRowIsRefusedAndAuditsNothing` in `AdminDepartmentsEndToEndTest` and `AdminJobTitlesEndToEndTest`: each posts to an id no row has, reads `error=no_data` on the redirect, and asserts the audit table gained nothing for that target type. The department and job title tests also pin their save's `error_db`, so the two behaviours stay distinct. `anUnchangedSaveAndARepeatDeleteStillFlashTheirSuccess` (D-253) still passes on all four pages, which is what keeps the refusal from swallowing a no-op; #293's review round 1 proved it pins that by tightening all four soft deletes to `AND is_active = 1`, which fails exactly those four tests. **Evidence.** Five cases, each with every file restored byte-identical after its run. With `main`'s four services and four controllers, exactly the four new tests fail. Two mutants that ignore the count again fail exactly the tests that pin them: the branch save (the branches test), and all four deletes (all four tests). One case is a negative control: auditing before the refusal instead of after changes nothing, because `recordAction` is `MANDATORY` (ADR-0015) and the refusal rolls its row back with the write. The fifth case shows what the audit assertion really rests on: with `recordAction` switched to `REQUIRES_NEW` as well, the row survives the refusal and the branches test fails. |
| Rollback | Revert the merge. Nothing is stored differently; a write that matched no row wrote nothing before either, beyond its audit row. |
| Related | **#286**, #285, D-253, R-044, #215. |

## D-268: The Employees Window Is Legacy's Four Sections, Its Row Actions Ask What Legacy Asks, And An Approved Join Request Opens The Employee Form

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | Proposed 2026-09-20 in the pull request for #216's employees and join requests findings; accepted when the repository owner merges it. |
| Decision | **The window's shape.** `employees.jte` renders `_employee_form.php` as legacy lays it out: the form is `org-form-grid-wrap`, and inside it four `emp-form-section org-form-span-2` blocks, each an `emp-form-section__title` over an `org-form-grid` -- personal data (`:72`), job details (`:161`), mobile attendance (`:218`) and, on the add path only, salary data (`:232`). The phone, country code and password sit in legacy's `emp-login-credentials` block under `employee_mobile_login_hint`, in its three-cell grid, with legacy's `minlength="6"` and its `password_field_hint` placeholder, and `password_optional` beside the input on an edit (`:90-114`). The port rendered one flat column of `form-row`s, so every rule in `employee-form.css` and the two-column rule in `org-form.css` -- both legacy's byte for byte -- matched nothing on this page. **The salary section** is legacy's ten components (`:231-283`): the basic salary `required` and labelled `(Mandatory)`, then transport, food, risk, incentives, insurance, tax, advances, fund and penalty labelled `(Optional)`, each `step="0.01" min="0" value="0"`, split into `entitlements` and `deductions` under `emp-form-subtitle` headings in an `emp-salary-grid`. `AdminEmployeesController` and `EmployeeStore.insertSalaryContract` already read and wrote all ten; the window offered a field for one, so the other nine could only ever be stored as zero. Legacy's edit never shows the section, and neither does this. **The close and the button.** The window carries `page.php:383,398`'s `modal-close` ×, and the submit button says `add_employee` on an add and `save` on an edit (`_employee_form.php:286`), where the port always said Save. **The row actions** follow `employee_helper.php:671-686`: deactivate is a `row-actions__item--danger` behind `confirm_delete`, legacy's own prompt for it, and reactivate a `row-actions__item--success` that asks nothing. Both were plain items that asked nothing, so deactivating an employee took one click with no prompt. **An approved join request** goes to `employees.php?action=edit&id=<id>` (`home_service.php:669-673`), because a join request carries a name and a phone and nothing else; the port returned to the list. A refusal still returns to the list it was made from (`join_requests/page.php:8-10`), and the guards, the audit row and the `approved_ok` flash are unchanged. **The request date** is `home_format_datetime()` (`home_service.php:1043-1072`) -- the day, the month's name, the year and a twelve-hour time, Arabic with ص and م -- where the port printed the stored timestamp with its `T` swapped for a space. **The actions-disabled banner** is the employees page's own, on a page that hides both of its decisions behind the switch (D-161) and said nothing when it was off. |
| Why | #216's employees and join requests audit, re-checked line by line against `505004f`. Two of the audit's claims were wrong and are recorded here as already done: `employee-form.js` is loaded and the edit window does pre-fill, and the country select lists exactly what legacy's does -- `company_country_codes()` is `phone_country_codes_for_select()` (`company_helper.php:31-34`), which is what `PhoneCountryChoices` implements (D-261). |
| Divergences from legacy | **The branch field.** Legacy labels it "(optional)" and hints that an employee with no branch may check in at any of the company's; neither is true here, because the column is NOT NULL and the save refuses a missing branch (R-055) where legacy's writes NULL. Neither the suffix nor the hint is copied, and the template says why. **The last name.** Legacy's input is `required` with a `*`; the port's is not. Legacy's server checks only the first name, and its own rows -- a join request stores one name (R-019) -- would be unsaveable through a form that insisted on a last one. **Field ids.** Legacy's salary inputs are `sal_basic` to `sal_penalty`; the port's ids are the field names, as every other input in this form already is (`first_name`, `branch_id`, …). Only `<label for>` reads them. **An approval under a company filter.** An administrator filtered to one company who approves another company's request lands on the employees list rather than the window: `DashboardOrgScope.canOpenRow` refuses a row outside the filter (D-176), and legacy's page has no such rule. Under that filter the row is not on screen, so this is reachable only with a crafted id, and the approval itself still succeeds -- R-061's difference, unchanged. |
| Also changed | `HomeDisplay.dateTime` is `home_format_datetime()` rather than the stored timestamp cut to sixteen characters. Its Javadoc had claimed to be that function while doing something else, and it is what legacy calls in all three places this port prints the value: the join requests page (`join_requests/page.php:57`), the home page's activity feed (`home_service.php:1079`) and its complaints panel (`dashboard/index.php:160`). Legacy calls it a fourth time, at `dashboard/index.php:242`, for the join-requests panel on its own home page, which this dashboard does not render. Both home cells now read "20 سبتمبر 2026 2:30 م" or "Sep 20, 2026 2:30 PM", and a missing value is the em dash legacy prints where the feed printed nothing. `AttendanceDisplay.parse` and `ListDisplay.trim` are public so the `home` package can reuse them; neither behaves differently. The complaints panel's `meta.isEmpty()` branch is now unreachable, because the formatter never returns an empty string; it is kept because `index.php:162`'s `$cpMeta !== ''` is unreachable in legacy for the same reason. `AdminPageStylesheetTest`'s `UNSTYLED_IN_LEGACY_TOO` gains `emp-login-credentials`, `emp-login-credentials__country` and `emp-login-credentials__phone`, each checked against legacy's own `pages/employees/assets/employee-form.css`, which styles the hint, the grid and `__password .form-hint` and leaves the wrapper and those two cells to the grid. No store, query, message key or schema changes: every key this renders was already in both catalogues. |
| Not in this change | **The list's filters.** Legacy carries `employee_filter_query_params()` through the add link, each row's edit link, the form's cancel, the window's close and the redirect after a save (`page.php:189-190,661-665`, `_employee_form.php:285`); every one of the port's is a bare `/admin/employees`, and only the company survives, through `DashboardOrgScope.rememberAfterWrite`. That is how every ported list page behaves, so it is a change of its own rather than this page's. **A failed save.** Answering the audit's question: legacy does *not* keep the filters there either -- `page.php:32,37` redirects to a bare `employees.php?action=add`. It does reopen the window, where the port returns to the list with the error banner; both lose what was typed, because legacy's reopened window is empty too. **A browser will still submit a save with no branch**, which the service then refuses, losing the form: the select's empty choice is `value="0"`, which `required` accepts. That is the defect the shift select's `value=""` fixed, on the field beside it. It is not only the add path: this change sends an operator who approves a join request straight into the edit window for a row that has no branch yet, which is the likeliest way to meet it, and a refusal there returns to the list with the banner rather than reopening what was typed. **#300** tracks both halves. **`company-detail.jte` and `settings.jte`** still gate a control on the actions switch and show no banner; `AdminLayoutWiringTest` names them so the omission is recorded rather than assumed. |
| Regression coverage | `AdminEmployeesEndToEndTest` (66 tests) gains five: the four section titles in order and the close control, and only three of them on an edit; the salary section's ten labels, requirement suffixes, `step`, `min`, `value` and the basic salary's `required`, and its absence from the edit window; a contract written from the rendered window carrying all ten components as typed, read back from `salary_contracts`; the submit button's two words; and the deactivate item's prompt and danger class beside the reactivate item's success class and silence. `AdminJoinRequestsEndToEndTest` (19) gains the approval's redirect target, the window it opens and the flash it carries, and the request date in both languages at an afternoon time and at half past midnight; `theDecisionReturnsToTheFilterItWasMadeFrom` is now `aRefusalReturnsToTheFilterItWasMadeFrom`, because an approval no longer does. `HomeDisplayTest` (5) pins the formatter itself, including the twelve-hour rollover, the unpadded hour beside the padded minutes, a timestamp with no seconds, the em dash and the unreadable value legacy returns as it came. `AdminLayoutWiringTest` gains the banner gate. `employee-form-layout.spec.js` (browser project) draws the window with the template's nesting under the layout's sheets and the page's own, and measures it: two columns at 1440px and one at 390px for the section grid and the salary grid, three login cells and one, a span-2 row running the whole grid, the ruled section title, and no sideways scroll on a phone; its third test reads `employees.jte` and fails if the four sections are renamed, reordered or unnested. **Evidence** (`empform/evidence.json`, 11 cases, every file restored byte for byte and hash-checked): with `employees.jte` back at `origin/main`, exactly the five new employees tests failed of 66; with `join-requests.jte` and `AdminJoinRequestsController.java` back at `origin/main`, exactly the approval, the date and the banner gate failed of 34. Four mutants each failed exactly the tests pinning them: the nine salary components stored as zero; an approval returning to the join requests list; the twelve-hour clock keeping PHP's zero hour; and the deactivate item back to a plain item with no prompt. `HomeDisplay.dateTime` has no before-fix case of its own, because reverting it removes the signature `HomeDisplayTest` calls and the case would not compile; the third mutant covers it instead. Round 3 added three cases about the gate rather than about this page: two labels in one `.form-row` hidden behind a `data-dialog-class` div failed exactly the page-window test, the same behind a div whose class is one JTE expression carrying its own quotes failed exactly the row-window test, and both together with the gate's class reader put back to the pattern round 3 replaced failed nothing at all -- which is the defect, stated as a negative control. Round 4 added two: a label outside every `.form-row` wrapped in a `data-x-class="form-row"` decoy failed exactly the sibling sweep, and two labels sharing a row behind divs whose single-quoted attribute values contain a `class="..."` sequence failed exactly the row-window test. The second is unreachable today -- every `<div>` attribute under `src/main/jte/admin` is double-quoted -- and is fixed because the gate's job is to read the attribute, not to be right by luck. Afterwards those eight classes passed -- the two end-to-end classes, `HomeDisplayTest`, and the stylesheet, message-key, layout-wiring, table-convention and browser-spec-inventory gates -- 120 tests at `c1ea3da0` and **122 once `main` was merged in**, because #293 widened the message-key gate there; the `browser` project passed 104 and 111 respectively; six of the seven more are `main`'s new `company-detail.spec.js` and the seventh is the test `main` added to `employee-detail.spec.js`. Round 1 added a ninth class to that list: `AdminRowDialogButtonsTest`, which the window's composite login row broke. Its rule took three forms under review and this is the one that merged: a label belongs to the innermost element that is a cell around it, and two labels in one of those is the offence -- two directly in a `.form-row`, two in one classed element inside a `.form-row`, or two loose in a window with no `.form-row` at all. Round 1 read a label against any classed element anywhere, which released that last bucket; round 2 confined a cell to the inside of a row; round 3 fixed how the class attribute itself is read, because `data-dialog-class="x"` ended in `class="x"` on a word boundary and an all-expression class can render to nothing, so either could hide two labels behind an element that is not a cell; round 4 found the same loose reading still in the sibling sweep `everyLabelInARowWindowSitsInAFormRow`, where a `data-x-class="form-row"` decoy passed a label that sits in no row at all. Both sweeps share one reader now. It walks the tag's attributes in order rather than matching the text -- a name, then a quoted value whose quotes and braces belong to any `${...}` around them -- so a `class="..."` sequence inside another attribute's value is not this element's class, and an attribute that never closes fails rather than reading as unclassed. **Not covered:** the home page's two cells that `HomeDisplay.dateTime` feeds are pinned by the formatter's own unit tests and by nothing that renders them, so the `"ar".equals(lang)` wiring in `home.jte` is untested in either language; the join requests page's cell is tested in both. #299 tracks it. |

## D-269: The Requests Table, Its Filter And Its Decision Windows Are Legacy's, And Leave Balances Exports Again

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | Proposed 2026-09-20 in the pull request for #216 (the requests and leave balances pages) and #211; accepted when the repository owner merges it. |
| Decision | **The requests table is legacy's twelve columns** (`requests/page.php:65-78`): number, code, name, type, from and to date, from and to time, notes, reply, status, actions. The port carried a thirteenth, the request's registration date, which legacy builds no header and prints no cell for (`:119-132`); it is gone, and the empty row's `colspan` counts twelve with it. The reply header asks for `decision_reply`, legacy's own key (`:75`), rather than `admin_reply`. **The status filter leads with "all"**, as `hr_render_labeled_select()` is called (`:101-107`), before pending, approved and rejected; the page still defaults to pending, because it is a queue rather than an archive. **The search box** carries `requests_search_placeholder` (`:89`), the entry already in both catalogues, instead of the generic "search…". **Both decision windows** label their box `decision_reply` followed by `(optional)` and carry legacy's placeholder, the same label followed by an ellipsis (`:152-156`), where the port used `reply` -- a different entry, "رد" rather than "الرد" -- and said nothing about the reply being optional. **Leave balances exports again** (`leave_balances/page.php:7-9, 104`): a green link beside the add button, carrying the filters the pager carries, and `GET /admin/leave_balances?export=csv` answers with the spreadsheet `csv_export_send()` sends -- every row the filter admits rather than the page on the screen, ordered by the employee's name (`hr_list_helper.php:1012-1048`), the six translated headers, and `LegacyXlsxWriter` for the bytes. |
| Why | #216's audit of the two pages. Three of the five were visible on every page load: a column the dashboard it replaces does not have, an "all" option below three others where legacy puts it first, and a missing export -- the one thing on the leave balances page that produces a file, absent since the page was ported. |
| Divergences from legacy | **The button says CSV and the file is a spreadsheet.** `csv_export_send()` rewrites its own `.csv` filename to `.xlsx` and sends the OOXML content type (`query.php:375-405`), which is `hr-legacy#23`. The bytes, the extension and the content type are reproduced, so what #23 asks for -- that they agree with each other -- already holds; only the button's wording is legacy's, and relabelling it is the owner's call, not this port's. **The company column** stays for an administrator with no company filter: it is the port's own, and legacy has no such view. It is a thirteenth column on that view, and it renders fourth, straight after the employee's name (`requests.jte:124`), which is where the test now pins it. **The export link's query** is the port's `carry` order (`search`, `company_id`, `year`), the same set and order the pager on that page already uses, where `hr_list_query_params()` writes company first. **Two decision windows, not one.** Legacy retitles a single modal (`requests-actions.js`); the port keeps D-259's two, each with its own field id, and both now carry the same label and placeholder. |
| Also changed | **`EmployeeRequest.createdDate()`** is deleted with the cell that was its only caller; the record keeps `createdAt`, as it keeps `decidedAt`, because it mirrors the row `r.*` returns. **The penalties toolbar** asked for `leave_balances_search_placeholder`, a copy of the same defect being fixed on requests. It asks for `penalties_search_placeholder` now (`penalties/page.php:143`). Both entries carry identical text in both languages, so nothing on screen moves and no test can fail on it; it is fixed because the next translator to change one of them would find the wrong page changing. **The sweep is of one defect, not of every search field:** a page asking for another page's placeholder key. The attendance toolbar is a different and larger gap and is left alone -- `attendance.jte:100-101` renders no placeholder at all and labels the field `search`, where legacy labels it `employee_name` and places `att_search_placeholder` with its ellipsis inside (`includes/payroll_list_helper.php:96-101`); the key already exists in both catalogues. Adding the placeholder alone would leave that field half-matched, so it belongs to the attendance page's own change (#217), and **#303** records it. **`LeaveBalanceStore`'s `WHERE`** is now one private method the list and the export share, so the file cannot narrow differently from the table above it. **`leave-balances.jte`'s `carry`** is built before the card rather than after the table, because the export link needs it too. **R-073** said none of legacy's four dashboard exports is ported and that no decision covers them. One of the four is ported here, so the register named a scope that is no longer true: it now reads three, points its disposition at this entry, and keeps the owner's question open for `attendance`, `advances` and `penalties`, which this change deliberately does not take. |
| Not in this change | **The header key swap is invisible.** `admin_reply` and `decision_reply` both read "Reply" and "الرد" in both catalogues, here and in legacy's `lang.php`, so no test fails on the swap alone; what the new test pins is the twelve columns, their order and their text. **The toolbar's field order.** Legacy puts the dates before the selects on requests, advances and penalties alike (`requests/page.php:92-107`, `advances/page.php:174-188`, `penalties/page.php:146-159`); all three of the port's toolbars put the selects first. One page reordered on its own would make three pages disagree, so this is one change across the three, not a line in this one. **The `deduct_balance` badge** in the type cell and the grey and blue badges on the leave day counts have no legacy equivalent (`requests/page.php:123`, `leave_balances/page.php:116-118`, which print the plain value); they predate this change, nothing records them, and removing them is a visual decision for the owner. **The other three exports** legacy offers -- attendance, penalties and advances -- and the payroll run's. This page's is the first on the surface; the others are their own pages' work. |
| Regression coverage | `AdminRequestsEndToEndTest`: `theTableCarriesLegacysTwelveColumnsAndNotTheRegistrationDate` (the twelve headers in order, one cell per header, `colspan="12"` on the empty row, and, for an unfiltered administrator, all thirteen in order with the company column fourth), `theStatusFilterOffersAllFirstAndStillDefaultsToPending` (the four options in order, with the selected one, for no filter, `all` and `rejected`), `theSearchBoxCarriesLegacysPlaceholder`, and `bothDecisionWindowsLabelTheirReplyAsLegacyDoes` (both labels, both placeholders, neither box required). `AdminLeaveBalancesEndToEndTest`: `theExportLinkCarriesTheListsOwnFilters` (the link unfiltered and with a company and a search, encoded as the pager encodes them), `theExportSendsEveryFilteredRowAsLegacysSpreadsheet` (200, the OOXML content type, `leave_balances_2026.xlsx`, a real ZIP, the six headers and both rows by employee name with `per_page=1` on the URL), `theExportNeverReachesPastTheFilter` (Alpha's file holds Alpha alone; unfiltered holds both), and `anEmptyListStillExports`. **Evidence** (`requests-evidence.py`, `requests/evidence.json`): six cases, each exact. With all six production files at `origin/main` -- together, because main's `requests.jte` calls the accessor this change deletes -- exactly those eight tests failed and the other 43 passed. Five mutants each failed exactly the tests pinning them: no "all" option (1), no export button (1), the registration date column kept (1), the export narrowed by year alone (2, including the tenant one), and the export in the list's newest-first order (1). Every file restored byte for byte and hash-checked. Gates: `AdminPageStylesheetTest`, `AdminTemplateMessageKeyTest`, `AdminLayoutWiringTest`, `AdminTableConventionsTest`, `AdminTemplateIdsTest`, `AdminRowDialogButtonsTest`, `AdminRowActionVariantsTest`, `AdminFilterCascadeTemplateTest`, `AdminTenantGuardCoverageTest`, `AdminActionReachabilityTest`, `AdminPhpIntCastTest`, `AdminDashboardPageInventoryTest`, `PlatformAdminWebChainCoverageTest`, `AdminPenaltiesEndToEndTest` and `PlatformAdminFullFlowTest`. |
| Rollback | Revert the merge. Nothing is stored or migrated, and the export only reads: the one new query is a single `SELECT` over `leave_balance` joined to `employees`, on the same `WHERE` the list already runs, with no `LIMIT` because legacy has none. **Its size is not bounded by anything checked:** the intended shape is one row per employee per year, but `leave_balance` has no unique key on `(employee_id, year)` and neither insert path refuses a duplicate, so the employee count is an assumption rather than a ceiling, and nothing here was measured. **#302** carries the two read-only counts that would settle it. This is the second time a figure in this area has been asserted from a comment rather than measured -- D-244's "A correction to D-241" row, which withdrew "3,783 active employees" for the same reason and replaced the comment it came from -- so the number is left out rather than restated. If it fails, the operator gets the dashboard's error page instead of a download and the request shows in the access log as a 500 on `/admin/leave_balances?export=csv`; nothing is written either way. |
| Related | **#216** (requests, leave balances), **#211**, hr-legacy#23, D-259 (the row windows), D-263 (the year cast), R-046. |

## D-270: The Four Org Pages' Markup And Option Order Are Legacy's, The Branch Form's Ids Are Too, And `classesOf` No Longer Misreads A Template Expression

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | Proposed 2026-09-20 in the pull request for #298, #304, #211 and #216; accepted when the repository owner merges it. |
| Decision | Branches, departments, job titles and shifts brought to legacy's markup where they diverged. **Branches:** the row actions now read Edit, Delete, QR (`org_helper.php:849-857`), where the port read Edit, QR, Delete. The QR panel is legacy's own modal -- `modal-bg open > modal modal--org-form modal--branch-qr` (`_branch_qr_modal.php:1`) -- instead of a `data-table-card` in the page flow; its active block now orders status, image, then meta in `<strong dir="ltr">` (`:96-105`), and its "no code" state carries `branch-qr-status`, not `branch-qr-meta`. `br_qr_expires` is prefilled as `org_branch_qr_expires_input_value()` prefills it: the current expiry while a code is active, or today at 23:59 otherwise (`Branch.qrExpiresInputValue`). The form's `br_*` ids are restored (`br_name`, `br_address`, `br_lat`, `br_lng`, `br_radius`, `br_active`), `dir="ltr"` is added to latitude and longitude, and `step="1"` plus `dir="ltr"` to the radius. **Departments and job titles:** the unfiltered option label order is now legacy's `branch — company` / `department — company` (`org_helper.php:485-492`); the port read the two names swapped, in both the filter and (job titles) the form select. The job title department cell's stray `text-muted` is dropped (`job_titles/page.php:149` carries no class). **Shifts:** the start and end `<th>` carry `col-center`, and their cells are `col-center dir="ltr"` plain text with an em dash for a null or empty time (`org_shift_time_display()`, `Shift.startTimeDisplay`/`endTimeDisplay`), replacing the badges the port drew for what are `<input type="time">` values, not counts. The empty row's `colspan` is `9`/`8`, correcting an off-by-one (`shifts/page.php:79` reads `9 : 8`; the port read `8 : 7`). The add form's name label reads `shift_name`, not `shift` (`_shift_form.php:17`; both catalogues already carry `shift_name`). The row number carries no class, dropping a `text-muted` neither shifts' own number nor branches'/departments'/job titles' carries. **`AdminRowDialogButtonsTest`'s `classesOf`** (D-259's gate, which the QR modal's new `.modal-bg` window now reaches) is fixed for #304's two defects: it is seeded with `int from = 0` rather than `tag.indexOf(' ')`, so a tab- or newline-separated attribute is found, where `\s` in `ATTRIBUTE`'s own pattern already accepted one; and a JTE expression inside a `class` value is now replaced with `U+FFFF`, a noncharacter no template can contain, rather than deleted outright, so `form-row${x}` and `${x}form-row` no longer read as holding the standalone class `form-row` -- the render could leave a different, glued token instead. A value built only of markers, with no literal text at all, still reads as no class, which is unchanged and keeps the existing `class="${row.cssClass()}"` shape hiding an offence rather than inventing one. |
| Why | The audit for #211/#216, verified at file:line against legacy `505004f` and the port; several of the audit's items were already correct and are recorded as such below rather than touched. #304's two `classesOf` defects are fixed because the QR modal is a new `.modal-bg` window that gate now parses. |
| Divergences from legacy | **The radius input's `inputmode="numeric"`.** Not legacy's: `_branch_form.php:30` carries no `inputmode` at all. It is kept because the two fields beside it already carry the port's own non-legacy `inputmode="decimal"`, and a radius field that opens a letter keyboard on a phone beside two that open a number one is worse than either choice made consistently. `step="1"` makes it an integer, so `numeric` rather than `decimal` is the right one. Removing all three is a separate decision about the port's mobile affordances, not this change's. |
| Also changed | **A window the server renders open now takes focus.** `modal-a11y.js` watched for the `open` class being *added*, which is how `crud.js` opens a window -- so a window the server renders with `open` already on it never fired the observer: focus stayed on the page behind the overlay, and the Tab trap only engages once focus is already on the window's first or last control, so Tab walked the page underneath. Legacy renders these itself (`?action=edit`, `?action=qr`), so it was the normal path for them. The script initialises an already-open window on load, which fixes all nine at once. `row-dialog.spec.js` gains the case -- focus lands inside, Tab from the last control stays inside and never reaches the link behind, Escape closes -- and removing the initialiser fails exactly it, 18 of 19. Codex raised this on the pull request; the round-1 reviewer had read the same source and concluded the trap held, which was half right: Escape is a document-level handler and does work, the trap is in the same handler but only fires at the window's own first and last control. **The QR window says it is a dialog** -- `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"` and `aria-labelledby` on its heading, as `rowDialog.jte:40` writes them and as legacy writes nowhere. Eight other server-opened windows still carry none; `AdminLayoutWiringTest.aServerOpenedWindowSaysItIsADialog` names them in a list that can only shrink, and **#306** carries them page by page. Both window rules read a class that *can* render `open`, not only one written `open` literally: `companies.jte` and `banners.jte` build it conditionally (`class="modal-bg${formOpen ? " open" : ""}"`) and were invisible to both rules while they matched the literal alone (round 2). Eleven windows match now. The Cancel rule skips the two whose whole window sits inside an actions gate -- `banners.jte` inside `@if(canWrite)`, `companies.jte` inside `@if(actionsEnabled)` -- because with the switch off there is no window at all to escape from; nine remain and all nine pass, and both of the conditional ones already carry the dialog semantics. Round 3 found that match still keyed on a fixed prefix, so a window whose `class` is not its first attribute was invisible and `open` in any other attribute enrolled one; rewriting it broke the built-class case in turn, which the `companies.jte` mutant caught before it was committed. `TemplateText.rawClassOf` is what holds both: it reads the class attribute wherever it sits and keeps its expressions, answering what the class *could* be, where `classesOf` answers what it *certainly* is. **Correction, round 4:** the earlier sentence here said round 2's widening "never worked" and that `companies.jte` and `banners.jte` "stayed invisible" at `cbcc20e5`. That was false, and the reviewer proved it by replaying `cbcc20e5`'s own matcher over `cbcc20e5`'s own templates: the committed form took the literal prefix and asked whether the text up to the first `>` contained `open`, which matched both. The form that could not see them was an intermediate one in the working tree, never committed. The defect round 3 fixed was real; the history this entry gave for it was not. Both rules also strip comments first: a comment naming `t.apply("cancel")` satisfied the Cancel rule for a window whose Cancel had been deleted. `AdminTemplateIdsTest`, `AdminRowActionVariantsTest`, `AdminRowDialogButtonsTest` and these rules strip, all four through `TemplateText` -- `withoutComments` for a gate that reports a file, `blankComments` for one that reports a line. **#307** carries the seven that still do not, two of which round 5 added to it: `AdminPhoneFormTemplateTest`, whose own `@if`/`@endif` depth walk reads raw text, and `AdminClockUsageTest`, whose direction is the opposite -- a `LocalDate.now()` written in a comment is reported as an offence. Its live instance is `AdminPageStylesheetTest`, and round 4 corrected what that instance is: `class="content"` is never collected, because `collectIncludes` excludes `layout` from every page's reached set; `class="pager"` is, out of the comment at `pager.jte:7`, and it passes not because a stylesheet defines it -- nothing defines `.pager` -- but because `pager` sits on `UNSTYLED_IN_LEGACY_TOO`. The eighteen pages that render a pager are each credited with a class no template writes. The readers are one reader now, `TemplateText`, because each had been written separately and each was wrong in its own way about the same two facts. Round 4 found that claim ahead of itself -- `AdminTemplateIdsTest` still carried its own copy when it was made -- so all four gates call it now and `TemplateTextTest` pins the reader itself. That test exists because the gates cannot test it: each asks it only about the templates that exist, so a reader that stops seeing a shape no template currently writes leaves every gate green, which is how `rawClassOf`, reverted to the pattern it replaced, left the reviewer's `--tests 'com.workin.backend.*'` run at 937 tests across 100 classes with no failure. **Round 4 found the Cancel rule knew one spelling of the gate it is named after.** It scanned a window for `@if(canWrite)` only, so a Cancel wrapped in `@if(actionsEnabled)` -- the switch itself, thirteen live occurrences across six templates -- passed it green, which is round 1's defect reachable again by the other spelling. Both are scanned now. Three smaller things went with it: `insideAGate` ended the gate's arm at the first `@else` in the file rather than the gate's own, so any ordinary conditional written inside the gate before the window dropped that window out of the arm (it walks to the `@else` at depth 1 now, and the third gate string, which matched nothing in any template, is gone); `modal-bg` and `open` were matched as substrings, so `modal-bg-open` or `dropdown-open` would have enrolled a window the server never opens, and both are whole-token patterns now; and `rawClassOf`, which since round 3 runs over every div in every admin template, aborted on an unterminated attribute with a message naming no file, so it takes the path and names it. Round 4's structural suggestion -- one scanner returning a block's arms, replacing `endOfBlock`, `depthAt` and the inline `@else` walk, tested directly rather than through the templates -- is **#308**: the narrow fix is here with its evidence case, and the rewrite of the gate that guards this change's own subject is not taken in a change already four rounds long. **Round 5 stopped the rule enumerating spellings.** A literal list of two gate strings had served two scans whose safe directions are opposite -- a missing entry hides a gated Cancel, an extra entry skips a window entirely -- and the templates already wrote a third spelling the list did not hold, `@if(canWrite && ...)`, four times. The Cancel scan now reads every `@if`'s **condition**: one that names the switch is a gate whatever else it says, and the condition's polarity decides which arm is the gated one, because under `@if(!canWrite)` it is the `@else` arm that needs the switch on. A condition naming the switch both ways is not guessed at -- it fails with the file and the condition named. `insideAGate` stays narrow on purpose and skips only a window whose gate **is** the switch, and the two share the `@else`-at-depth-1 walk rather than a list. Round 5 also found the in-window scan spanning the whole block including the `@else` arm, so a Cancel written correctly there -- rendering exactly when the switch is off -- turned the gate red on a correct template; that arm walk is shared now, and the control case in the evidence keeps it green. And the window scan read an expression's **code**: `class="modal-bg${row.open() ? 'a' : 'b'}"` enrolled a window because a method is named `open`. `TemplateText.possibleClassText` keeps a class value's literal text and the string literals inside its expressions -- what can actually reach a browser -- and drops the code; a value that is wholly unknown (`${state}`) still reads as not-a-window, which is the silent direction and is stated as a trade rather than an oversight. **#308** carries the scanner rewrite these walks keep asking for, and round 5 added the fourth walk to it, in `AdminPhoneFormTemplateTest`. **Round 6 replaced the polarity check with an evaluation.** Round 5 decided which arm a condition gates by asking whether a `!` sat immediately before the switch's name, and one pair of parentheses defeated it in both directions at once: `@if(!(canWrite))` hid a gated Cancel and failed a correct template. The condition is now evaluated with the switch off and every other operand unknown, in three values -- `FALSE` means the `@if` arm cannot render and is the gated one, `TRUE` means the `@else` arm cannot, and unknown means neither arm is the switch's to hide, which is what `@if(canManage && !actionsEnabled)` is. The refusal to guess is narrower for it: a condition naming the switch both ways is now read correctly rather than refused, and an operand that holds the switch inside something larger (`canWrite == true`) fails with the file, the condition and the remedy named -- but only when its block holds the control, because round 7 found such a condition anywhere in a window failing the whole gate over a block this rule has no business reading. Round 6 also found both the condition reader and the class reader blind to string literals: `@if(name.equals(")") && canWrite)` truncated at the bracket inside the string and the switch beside it went unseen, and `possibleClassText` stopped at an escaped quote, dropping a class the render can produce -- the silent direction. Both read strings now, escapes included. The loud direction it also named is kept and stated in the test rather than fixed: a string an expression only *compares* against (`${row.state().equals("open") ? "a" : ""}`) is read as text the class can render, which can enrol a window that is never open; the rule then asks that window for a Cancel and dialog semantics, which is a failure someone reads. **Round 7 found the rule reading two arms of a chain and not the rest.** It read an `@if`'s own arm and its `@else`, so a Cancel in an `@elseif` arm that needs the switch on was invisible -- and `@elseif` is written fourteen times across eleven admin templates, `@elseif(canWrite)` at `settings-templates.jte:113`, with the QR window itself carrying an `@if`/`@elseif`/`@else` chain. The rule reads **every** arm of a block now: an arm is out of reach with the switch off when its own condition cannot hold, or when an earlier one certainly does, and the `@else` when any earlier condition certainly holds. Round 8 then found that walk reading **two** arms as well: it counted depth from the previous arm, which leaves the block's own `@if` outside the region, so every third and later arm read as depth 0 -- in a commit whose title says a chain has as many arms as it has conditions, and with eight live blocks of three or more arms, one of them inside the QR window itself. The depth is counted from the block now, and two synthetic shapes pin the third arm in both directions. The two helpers that read an `@if` and its `@else` are deleted rather than left beside it: the evidence case that had pinned them went green when the rule stopped calling them, which is the harness reporting dead code as plainly as it reports a defect. **Codex raised a third thing about the same modal on this head**, and it is answered rather than restructured: with the switch off the expiry field still renders inside a real POST form while only the submit is gated, so the field can be filled and submitted from the keyboard. That is the shape `branch-form.jte:25` has always had -- the sibling this page's Cancel rule is modelled on -- and it is a convention question for both files rather than this page's own defect (**#310**). What this change does add is the pin for what happens then: `generateQr()` refuses at its `gate()` before the store is touched, `PlatformAdminCompanyActionDisabledTest` seeds a branch and asserts the refusal and that `qr_code` stays null, and an evidence case removes the `gate()` and fails exactly it. **Round 10 found two differences in the modal itself**, which is the first page markup any round has found wrong since round 1. Legacy writes `class="btn btn-blue"` for the generate/regenerate submit (`_branch_qr_modal.php:40`) and the port had carried `btn-yellow` since its original commit, through this change's own rewrite, with the divergences row saying there was only one; it is `btn-blue` now and the modal test asserts it. Four other pages write the same yellow where legacy writes blue -- `assets`, `advances`, `penalties` and `leave-balances`, each a `save` -- and that is **#309**, with the observation that no gate reads a submit's variant the way `AdminRowActionVariantsTest` reads a row action's. And legacy's active arm is `$qrActive && $qrImage !== ''` where the port asked only `qrActive`: `qrActive` is `empty()`-based, so a code that is blank but not empty is active to it, while `qrImageUrl` trims and returns nothing -- the port rendered the active block with an empty image source where legacy renders the expired state. Only a hand-edited row reaches it, which is the standard `qrActive` already holds for a code of `"0"`. The arm asks both halves now. **Round 9 found the block counting itself too narrow, in two ways that are live.** jte gives `@for` an `@else` of its own for the empty collection, and the counting knew only `@if`/`@endif` -- so a `@for(...) ... @else ... @endfor` written above a Cancel inside `@if(canWrite)` ended the gate's arm at the loop's `@else`, and the Cancel read as ungated. Three of the nine windows this rule checks already contain a `@for`. And jte accepts `@if (cond)` with a space, which the counting did not match while still matching its `@endif`, so a spaced `@if` nested inside a correctly written gate left an unpaired `@endif`, truncated the block, and made the rule skip it. One pattern covers all of it now -- `@if`, `@for`, `@endif`, `@endfor`, each with optional space -- and the three bypasses are evidence cases. **The dialog rule also only asked that `aria-labelledby` be present**, never that it names something the window writes an id for; Codex raised it, all three live targets resolve, and the rule now resolves them rather than trusting the attribute -- matching the id as an attribute rather than as text, since `data-dialog-id="x"` ends in `id="x"`. `aDialogsNameResolvesInsideItsOwnWindow` pins the six shapes the templates cannot ask it, because all three live windows resolve and the rule was green while a name pointing at nothing would have been. **`AdminTemplateIdsTest` read a comment as markup.** A comment added here named the id it was adding, two lines above the attribute itself, and the gate counted the pair as one page writing one id twice -- turning CI's `test` job red for a page that renders exactly one. It strips `<%-- --%>` before scanning now, as `AdminRowDialogButtonsTest` already did; a real second element carrying the same id still fails it. **The expiry test dated from the JVM's clock**, not the database's: with the JVM in UTC and legacy at UTC+2 the two disagree from 22:00 UTC, so it would have failed for two hours a day. It reads `LegacyClock` now, through a stood-up request because the bean is request-scoped. Codex raised that one too. **The branch QR window's Cancel is outside the actions gate**, as `branch-form.jte:87-92` has always kept its own. Review round 1 found it inside: the window is a full-viewport overlay the server renders from `?action=qr&id=N`, the link that opens it is not gated, and `app.platform-admin.actions.enabled` ships **false** -- so the shipped default was an overlay with no visible way out. `crud.js` closes it on the backdrop and `modal-a11y.js` on Escape, but nothing on screen says either. `AdminLayoutWiringTest` gains the rule for the class rather than the instance: every window written `modal-bg open` **has** a Cancel, and none keeps it behind `@if(canWrite)`. Both halves are asserted because the second alone is vacuous -- Codex pointed out that the first form passed a window whose Cancel was deleted outright, which is the same defect by a shorter route. The nine such windows pass; the row dialogs and add modals are deliberately outside it, because they are written `modal-bg` with no `open` and the control that opens them is behind the same gate, so with the switch off they never appear at all. |
