## D-271: The Penalties And Advances CSV Exports Are Legacy's Spreadsheet, Reproducing #23 Again

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | Proposed 2026-09-21 in the pull request for #219 and #211; accepted when the repository owner merges it. |
| Decision | **Two of R-073's three remaining exports are ported.** `GET /admin/penalties?export=csv` (`penalties/page.php:12-14` calling `hr_export_penalties_csv()`, `hr_list_helper.php:1050-1088`) and `GET /admin/advances?export=csv` (`advances/page.php:11-13` calling `hr_export_advances_csv()`, `hr_list_helper.php:1110-1152`) each answer with the spreadsheet `csv_export_send()` sends (`query.php:375-405`), a green link beside each page's add button, offered to anyone who can open the page (`penalties/page.php:169`, `advances/page.php:198`) rather than gated on `canWrite`. **Penalties**: every row the filter admits -- company, `applied`, `date_from`, `date_to`, `search` -- in the same order the table uses (`pen.penalty_date DESC, pen.id DESC`), seven columns (`emp_code`, `employee_name`, `penalty_type`, `penalty_days`, `penalty_reason`, `penalty_date`, `applied_payroll`), filename `penalties_<date_from>_<date_to>.xlsx` with `all` standing in for either date when blank. **Advances**: every row the filter admits -- company, `status`, `date_from`, `date_to`, `search` -- ordered by `created_at DESC, id DESC`, which is also the order of the table above it once the list was corrected (see below), eight columns (`emp_code`, `employee_name`, `advance_amount`, `remaining`, `request_date`, `advance_reason`, `rejection_reason`, `status`), filename `advances_<today>.xlsx`. Both exports run through one private `where()` each store now shares between `paginate()` and `exportRows()` (D-269's shape for `LeaveBalanceStore`), so the file cannot narrow differently from the table above it. All values are read as the database renders them -- `penalty_days` as `decimal(5,1)` (`"0.5"`, `"1.0"`), `amount`/`remaining` as `decimal(10,2)` (`"1000.00"`) -- with a null `reason`/`rejection_reason` blank rather than the string `"null"`. |
| Why | #219 (R-073): three of legacy's four dashboard exports had no counterpart; D-269 ported one (leave balances). This closes two more, leaving only `attendance`. |
| Corrected while porting | **The advances list was ordered by the wrong column.** `hr_paginate_advances()` (`hr_list_helper.php:372`) orders by `a.created_at DESC, a.id DESC` and `hr_export_advances_csv()` (`:1150`) orders the same way; the port's `paginate()` had `a.request_date DESC` since `99a630b3`, recorded nowhere, so the table's order differed from legacy's whenever the two dates disagree. Review round 1 of this change found it -- and found this entry and the pull request describing the divergence as **legacy's**, which it is not. `paginate()` orders by creation now, the test seeds the two dates opposed (the only shape that can tell the columns apart) and asserts the page and the file, and two evidence cases put each `ORDER BY` back. **The penalties page's default range is not corrected here** and is **#312**: legacy defaults `date_from`/`date_to` to the current month (`penalties/page.php:9-10`) and the port defaults neither, so the first screen -- and now the unfiltered download -- is all history rather than this month. It is pre-existing in the merged `page()` controller and it governs an unpaginated file, which is why it is filed rather than left as a line here. |
| Divergences from legacy | **The button says CSV and the file is a spreadsheet**, exactly as D-269 records for leave balances: `csv_export_send()` rewrites its own `.csv` name to `.xlsx` and sends the OOXML content type (`hr-legacy#23`); the bytes, extension and content type are reproduced together, so #23's own ask already holds, and only the label is legacy's. **The export link's query** is the port's own `carry` order (`search`, `company_id`, then the page's own filter, then `date_from`/`date_to`), the same set the pager on that page already uses, rather than `hr_list_query_params()`'s company-first order. **Two pages' `carry` now also holds `date_from`/`date_to`.** Neither did before this change -- the pager and the page-size form silently dropped the date range on every page turn, a pre-existing gap this port does not otherwise touch. Legacy's own `$listQuery` always carries both (unconditionally for penalties, which defaults them to the current month; only when set for advances), and the export reuses whatever the page already resolves for `dateFrom`/`dateTo` -- so leaving the gap open would have made a filtered export silently widen on the very click that is supposed to reproduce the screen. Fixing it is the smaller risk, and it is one line added to a map this change was already relocating. **Neither page defaults `date_from`/`date_to` when absent**, unlike legacy, which defaults penalties' to the current month (`penalties/page.php:9`) and advances' to none at all. That divergence predates this change -- the port's `page()` controllers already read a blank string rather than legacy's default -- and is not this task's to fix; the export reuses exactly the value the list already resolves, defaulted or not, so the two never disagree with each other even though the port disagrees with legacy on what "no filter" defaults to. |
| Also changed | **`PenaltyStore`'s and `AdvanceStore`'s `WHERE`** are each now one private method `paginate()` and `exportRows()` share, extracted from what was inline `StringBuilder` code in `paginate()` alone. **`penalties.jte`'s and `advances.jte`'s `carry`** are built before the card rather than after the table, because the export link needs it too (the same relocation D-269 made for `leave-balances.jte`). **R-073** read three exports remaining; it now reads one (`attendance`), and its disposition points at this entry for the two closed here. |
| Not in this change | **`attendance`'s export** -- the third and last of R-073, and the one export helper `505004f` actually reworked (`payroll_export_attendance_csv()`); it is its own page's work. **#302** (export row count is unbounded and unmeasured) is the same risk these two exports inherit: neither query carries a `LIMIT`, matching legacy, and neither has been measured against a real row count. Not settled here -- #302 already carries it for leave balances and now covers all three ported exports. **The pager's own carry gap** on every other page that has one (if any) is not swept; only the two pages this change already touches gained `date_from`/`date_to`. |
| Regression coverage | `AdminPenaltiesEndToEndTest`: `theExportLinkCarriesTheListsOwnFilters`, `theExportSendsEveryFilteredRowAsLegacysSpreadsheet` (200, the OOXML content type, `penalties_all_all.xlsx` unfiltered, a real ZIP, the seven headers, both of one company's rows by `penalty_date`/`id` with `per_page=1`), `theExportNeverReachesPastTheFilter`, `anEmptyListStillExports`, `theExportAppliesTheDateRangeTheListApplies`. `AdminAdvancesEndToEndTest`: the same five, `theExportSendsEveryFilteredRowAsLegacysSpreadsheet` pinning the eight headers and `created_at`-ordered rows, `theExportAppliesTheStatusFilterTheListApplies` in place of the date test, and `theTableAndTheFileBothOrderByCreationAsLegacyOrdersThem`, which is the only test either order can fail: every other fixture seeds `request_date` and `created_at` in the same order, so the two columns produce the same rows. It seeds them opposed and asserts the page and the file. `AdminHrExportsWithActionsDisabledEndToEndTest` (new; `app.platform-admin.actions.enabled` at its default, `false`): both control-presence tests (the export anchor renders, the add button does not) and both endpoint tests (the export still answers 200 with the OOXML type), plus `theSwitchIsOffForThisContext` pinning the fixture. **Evidence** (`exports-evidence.py`, `exports/evidence.json`): eleven cases, each exact. `PenaltyStore.java` and `AdminPenaltiesController.java` reverted to `origin/main` together (the controller's `export()` calls `exportRows()`, absent on main's store, so the store cannot revert alone without breaking compilation) failed exactly the five tests naming that behaviour, and the equivalent pair for advances failed exactly its five; `penalties.jte`/`advances.jte` reverted alone each failed exactly their two rendering tests, and 24/24, 26/26 and 5/5 other tests passed throughout. Four mutants each failed exactly the tests pinning them: `PenaltyStore.exportRows()` and `AdvanceStore.exportRows()` each narrowed by `"1=1"` instead of the shared `where()` (three tests each -- the tenant, the date/status filter and the full-row assertion), and `penalties.jte`'s and `advances.jte`'s export anchor each moved inside `@if(canWrite)` (one test each, the switch-off render case). Three more cases go at what a whole-file revert cannot reach: `penalties.jte` carrying `date_from` but not `date_to` -- one half of a pair, where the export would narrow by a range open at one end -- `AdvanceStore.exportRows()` ordered by `request_date`, and `AdvanceStore.paginate()` back to `request_date`, each failing exactly one test. Every file restored byte for byte and hash-checked. Gates: `AdminPageStylesheetTest`, `AdminTemplateMessageKeyTest`, `AdminLayoutWiringTest`, `AdminTableConventionsTest`, `AdminActionReachabilityTest`, `AdminDashboardPageInventoryTest`, `AdminTenantGuardCoverageTest`, `PlatformAdminWebChainCoverageTest` and `PlatformAdminFullFlowTest`. |
| Rollback | Revert the merge. Nothing is stored or migrated; both exports only read, on the same `WHERE` each list already runs, with no `LIMIT` because legacy has none -- the same unmeasured-size risk D-269 recorded and #302 carries, now for three exports rather than one. If either fails, the operator gets the dashboard's error page instead of a download, and the request shows in the access log as a 500 on `/admin/penalties?export=csv` or `/admin/advances?export=csv`; nothing is written either way. |

## D-272: The Attendance Page's Toolbar, Headings, Pagers And Add Form Are Legacy's

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | Proposed 2026-09-21 in the pull request for #217's attendance page; accepted when the repository owner merges it. |
| Decision | `attendance/page.php` and the toolbar it draws (`payroll_render_attendance_filter_toolbar()`, `includes/payroll_list_helper.php:50-113`) row by row. **The toolbar** orders its fields branch, department, then the employee search, before the two dates, and that search is labelled `employee_name` and carries `att_search_placeholder` with the literal "..." legacy appends outside the key (`:96-101`); the port put the search first, labelled it `search`, and gave it no placeholder. **A branch option** reads "name — company" when no company is chosen and the name alone when one is, which is `org_option_label()` (`org_helper.php:485-492`) as `:81` calls it; the port printed the name alone in both views, so two branches of the same name in different companies were one word. ## D-273: The Admin Dashboard Stops Paying For Round Trips It Does Not Need

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | Proposed 2026-09-21 in its own pull request; accepted when the repository owner merges it. |
| Decision | **Two changes, both about the number of statements a page costs, neither changing what a page renders.** (1) `PlatformAdminSessionRevalidationFilter` **skips the `findById`, and nothing else, for `/admin/_assets/**`**: the filter chain's matcher is `/admin/**`, so every stylesheet, script and image on a page cost a reload against the legacy database, and `layout.jte` alone references eighteen of them before a page adds its own. The decision is a private `isAsset` predicate read on the raw path, inside `stillValid` and *after* the cap check, and it refuses to skip on anything the path could still mean something else -- a percent-encoding, a double slash, a traversal segment -- so it does not depend on the firewall in front of it having normalised the URI first. **The session's absolute cap is deliberately not skipped** (found on `24f57154`): an asset request carries the session cookie like any other, so it counts as activity, and skipping the whole filter -- as the first version did, via `shouldNotFilter` -- let a page that keeps fetching assets carry a session past a cap that is meant to be non-renewable by construction. (2) `OrgCascadeStore.cascade()` issues **one** statement instead of five: the five lists (branches by company, departments by company and by branch, job titles by department and by company) are unioned with a `part` discriminator and split in the store, with a single `ORDER BY part, grp, name, id` that reproduces each part's own order because every one of the five already ordered by its group then its name -- and the trailing `, id` decides what none of them decided, two names the collation cannot tell apart (see the next row). **The revalidation exception is scoped everywhere the rule is stated**, which took four review rounds to enumerate — the last of them found the two ADRs below: ADR-0015 prerequisite 9, `authorization-model.md` §5, `operations/monitoring-and-alerting.md`'s "Administrator deactivated but still active" row, `bootstrap/open-questions.md`'s deactivation note, and `PlatformAdminWebPrincipal`'s javadoc all say that "per request" means every request that can reach a controller. Checked and left alone: ADR-0010, ADR-0014, R-026, D-145 and `PlatformAdminWebSecurityConfig`'s comment are about `PlatformAdminAuthenticationFilter`, the bearer chain, which never serves these paths. **ADR-0016 and ADR-0018 do restate the rule in summary form**, which the round on `9a3bb528` corrected an earlier claim here about, so each now points at prerequisite 9 for the exception, and ADR-0015's own requirements bullet does too. |
| Why | Measured on the `compose.remote-db.yaml` stack, whose database is in another network: a round trip to it is **106 ms**, against about 0.3 ms to a container on the same host. At that latency a page's cost is its statement count, and the two biggest contributors were not the page's own queries. The asset filter charges the database roughly twenty times per page for data no asset uses; the cascade charges it five times for data one statement returns. Neither is visible on a local stack, which is why neither was found by looking at the code. |
| Divergences from legacy | None: no rendered byte changes. Legacy issues its own five queries for the same payload (`org_helper.php:337-449`); the port issuing one is not a behaviour difference, and the maps, their group keys and their order are asserted unchanged. **One order was never decided by anything before**: the collation is `utf8mb4_unicode_ci`, so two names that differ only in case or accents sort equal, and which of them came first was whatever the plan produced -- one plan per query then, one for the union now, and the two do not agree. The round on `75593319` measured that (`Tie`/`tie`/`TÍE` reorder). The union's `ORDER BY` ends `, id`, which **decides** it: collation-equal rows come back in id order, always, which is what the five queries were measured doing at the sizes anyone has looked at -- the round on `a3fcc4b9` found the old form's own tie order is plan-dependent once a tie group is large (500 rows), so for those there was no order to reproduce, only one to fix. `OrgCascadeQueryBudgetTest` seeds 64 rows sharing one name, which is enough that the sort does not come out in id order by accident: without the tiebreak that assertion fails. |
| Also changed | `accepted_lines`-style dead code: none. `OrgCascadeStore.grouped()` stays for `shiftsByCompany()`, which is one list and one query. |
| Not in this change | **The pool.** `app.legacy-db.*` is untouched; the connection count was re-read after the asset fix rather than raised to cover the traffic the fix removes. **Every other page's own queries**: this change touches the two costs that are paid by *every* page, not the per-page ones, and #302's unmeasured export size is unrelated and still open. **The 106 ms itself** is the network the customer's database is on; nothing here can shorten it. |
| Regression coverage | `PlatformAdminSessionRevalidationFilterTest`: `aStaticAssetIsServedWithoutRevalidating` (no interaction with the repository at all for an asset path) and `aPathThatMerelyBeginsLikeAnAssetIsStillRevalidated` (a traversal segment, a percent-encoding, a double slash, and `/admin/_assetsx/`, each still filtered), and from the round on `24f57154` **`anAssetRequestPastTheAbsoluteCapIsStillRefused`** (a session past the cap, on an asset path: the context cleared and the session invalidated **before the asset skip is reached**, because `capExceeded` is evaluated first -- so the cap decides the request, and `verifyNoInteractions(repository)` holds for that reason rather than because the path is an asset) and **`anAssetRequestWithNoEstablishmentStampIsRefused`**. `OrgCascadeQueryBudgetTest` (new, `com.workin.backend.perf`, on the real MariaDB, counting statements through the existing `QueryCounter`): the whole payload, an edit's kept rows and the administrator's unfiltered payload are each **one** statement, with each list's contents and order asserted beside the count. **Evidence** (`perf-evidence.py`, `perf/evidence.json`): five cases, each exact. Both production files reverted to `origin/main` in turn -- the filter failing exactly `aStaticAssetIsServedWithoutRevalidating`, the store failing exactly the three budget tests, which is what five statements look like. Three mutants: the filter's guards reduced to the prefix test (fails exactly the traversal test), the union's `ORDER BY` reversed (fails all three budget tests **and** `AdminEmployeesEndToEndTest`'s two payload assertions), and the last two parts of the union handed back swapped (fails the budget test and four of the employees page's). The round on `9a3bb528` adds the mutant the cap fix is actually about: `isAsset` evaluated **before** `capExceeded` in `stillValid`, which fails both new tests -- and the whole-filter revert to `24f57154`, which failed exactly those two (`expected: null but was: UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken[...]`) and nothing else. Every file restored byte for byte and hash-checked. |
| Rollback | Revert the merge; both changes are read-path only, with no migration, no stored state and no configuration. If the union query were wrong, every form's selects would be empty or mis-grouped -- visible immediately on any add or edit form, and caught by `AdminEmployeesEndToEndTest` before that. If the filter skip were wrong, a deactivated administrator would keep being served stylesheets until their next page request, which is the failure mode this decision accepts by name. An operator sees the difference as fewer rows in the legacy database's process list and a shorter page time; nothing new is logged, because nothing new happens. |
| Related | D-176 (company scope), R-051 (the cascade's payload size), D-250 (the kept rows an edit's maps carry), ADR-0015 prerequisite 9 (revalidate from the session's identifier), #302. |

## D-274: A Visit Blamed The Terminal For The Laptop's Wi-Fi, And Called The In/Out Column Unclear With The Answer Already On Disk

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | Proposed 2026-09-22 from the 2026-09-21 field runs against the terminal this repository calls `TERMINAL-A`; accepted when the repository owner merges it. |
| Decision | **Three changes, all reads.** (1) `ZkClient.connect()` retries a failed TCP connect **only** on `EHOSTUNREACH`, `ENETUNREACH` and `EHOSTDOWN` (`zk4370.TRANSIENT_CONNECT_ERRNOS`), three attempts two seconds apart. Those errnos fail instantly, so a terminal that is genuinely absent costs at most four extra seconds; a refusal or a timeout still raises on the first attempt, and the message is unchanged so the runbook's text still matches. One seam covers all three callers: `probe.zk_summary`, `sources.ZkSource.__enter__` (the agent's `once`) and `visit.zk_records`. (2) `probe` gains this laptop's own link as facts -- `arp_state()`, `wifi_link()`, `ping_facts()` and `laptop_network()` composing them, each taking its raw command output as an optional argument the way `lan_networks()` already does, and each reporting `None`/`unavailable` rather than a healthy-looking zero when the file or binary is absent. A visit whose read failed with one of those errnos now reports them and names **the laptop's network** as the remedy instead of sending the operator to open a device-compatibility finding; the numbers land in a new results-sheet row, `حالة الشبكة وقت المشكلة`. (3) `in_out_field()` takes the stored log's code distribution (`code_spread()`, a new sheet row `توزيع أكواد الدخول/الخروج في سجل الجهاز`): when the two watched punches cannot decide, the log's own shape can: everyone who comes in goes out again, so across thousands of records the in/out column is close to balanced while a column recording how people identified themselves is not. **The log never elects a column; it may only rule one out.** A column stands only when it is balanced (`IN_OUT_MINORITY_SHARE = 0.10`) **and** the other column has **at least two values** and is so one-sided across the whole log that it cannot be carrying in/out at all (`IN_OUT_CONSTANT_SHARE = 0.01`) -- a column with one value is what an unpressed in/out key looks like, so it rules nothing out; when both are balanced -- say 20 % and 5 % -- the answer stays `None`, because balance on its own is not evidence of meaning. `IN_OUT_LOG_MINIMUM = 200` records the floor below which a log cannot carry the argument at all. The same rule is printed by `doctor`, so the manual Mode B procedure decides `in_out_field` from it rather than from whether the last punch reads `1`. **The first rule written here was "a column that never changes cannot be the one", and the terminal's own backup refuted it**: `status` is not constant, it reads 1 in 11 424 records and 15 in two. Two records out of eleven thousand are somebody identifying themselves differently, not the branch going home; a rule counting distinct values would have called both columns live and reported the question unanswered on the very log that answers it. What was watched keeps precedence over the log; still-ambiguous is still `None`, but the finding now carries both distributions instead of one ambiguous pair. |
| Why | Two failures on the same visit, from one cause each. **The network one:** `cannot reach <device-ip>:4370 over TCP: [Errno 113] No route to host` is `EHOSTUNREACH` at `connect()` -- the kernel never resolved the hardware address, so no packet left and the terminal was never asked. The terminal read 11 422 records in step 4, read 11 424 half an hour later, and answers ping 120/120. The laptop was associated to the weakest of three access points sharing the branch's SSID (−66…−76 dBm, `CTRL-EVENT-BEACON-LOSS` at 19:43:09) and only roamed to the strong one (signal 100, channel 1) at 19:48:48, after the visit had ended; a two-minute ping to the terminal returned 120/120 **with nine duplicate replies and round trips from 0.89 ms to 441 ms**, which is what repeaters bridging one SSID look like. With `ucast_solicit=3 mcast_solicit=3 retrans_time_ms=1000`, one lost ARP exchange marks the neighbour `FAILED` and then *every* connect fails instantly until it is probed again -- which is why one fault produced two identical errors seconds apart, and why a bounded retry is the right size of fix. The report's remedy for the second was `اكتب الرسالة دي في الـ issue`: a laptop Wi-Fi fault filed against the model, where it would stay on the model's record. **The in/out one:** the terminal stored the check-out with the same two codes as the check-in (`punch=5, status=1` for both), so the two-punch method correctly refused to guess and the whole sheet stayed `—` -- while 11 424 records sat on the laptop in which `status` reads 1 every time and `punch` does not. |
| Measured, not assumed | `/proc/net/wireless`'s last column is **Missed beacon** and it read 0 throughout; the counter that actually climbed (403 → 529 over ten minutes) is `misc` under **Discarded packets**. `WIRELESS_COLUMNS` names all ten in the kernel's own order and a test pins that row, because a reader that takes the last column calls a link healthy while packets are dropping. |
| Also changed | `SHEET_ROWS` gained the two rows above, and `docs/devices/field-visit-runbook.md`'s appendix table gained the same two in the same positions -- `test_the_results_sheet_is_the_runbooks_appendix_row_for_row` is the gate that holds them together. `laptop_network` joins `networks` and `scan` as a collaborator injected into `Visit`, so the wiring is tested without patching modules. `probe.py`'s docstring now says it also reads an ICMP echo and two kernel files. |
| Not in this change | **The web page** (its own change, on top of this one): this is the field fix alone. **Windows' `ping`** counts with `-n` and prints another summary; `ping_facts` reports `unavailable` rather than parsing it, because a wrong `0%` would send an operator back to a terminal that is not the problem. **The errno is not threaded through `SourceError`/`DeviceResult`**: `unreachable_errno()` prefers the exception's own `errno`, including the chained `OSError`'s, and falls back to parsing a *already-flattened* string -- both `[Errno N]` and Windows' `[WinError N]`, mapped through `WINDOWS_TRANSIENT_CODES`. Threading a field through the agent's result types would be the wider change. **This row previously claimed the token is one "which Python writes and does not translate"**; review round 2 refuted exactly that -- Windows renders the same condition as `[WinError 10065]` -- and the code was fixed then while this sentence was not. **`READ_ONLY_COMMANDS` is untouched**; nothing here sends a terminal anything new. |
| Regression coverage | `tests/test_zk4370.py`: `test_a_lost_arp_exchange_is_retried_rather_than_ending_the_read` (the emulator behind two injected `EHOSTUNREACH` refusals), `test_a_terminal_that_stays_unreachable_is_still_the_same_error` (the attempt count and the unchanged message), `test_a_refused_connection_is_answered_not_retried` (the control: one attempt). `tests/test_visit.py`: `test_the_arp_state_is_read_for_the_address_asked_about` (past a `router` flag; one address is not another's prefix), `test_the_wifi_link_reads_the_column_the_driver_actually_moves`, `test_ping_counts_duplicates_and_never_invents_a_healthy_result` (the real 120/120/+9 summary, a lossy one, and Windows output refused), `test_the_laptop_network_pings_nothing_when_it_was_given_no_address`, `test_code_spread_counts_both_columns_across_the_log`, `test_the_log_decides_the_in_out_code_when_the_two_punches_cannot` (the real `(5,1)/(5,1)` pair with the real distribution; both columns varying and a too-short log still ambiguous; the watched pair keeping precedence), `test_only_an_errno_that_means_the_packet_never_left_counts`, and class `WhenTheLaptopNeverReachedTheTerminal` -- the remedy naming the laptop with its numbers and not the issue tracker, and a refusal keeping the terminal's own remedy. **Before/after:** against `HEAD`'s modules the same inputs give `fix='استنى شوية وشغّل الأمر تاني'`, no laptop-network row at all, and `in_out_field((5,1),(5,1),1) is None`; the three retry tests reproduce the field's own line, `ZkError: cannot reach …: [Errno 113] No route to host`, and `1 != 3` on the attempt count. ## D-275: The Site Visit Gets A Local Page, And Every Step Becomes Repeatable On Its Own

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | Proposed 2026-09-22; accepted when the repository owner merges it. |
| Decision | **`workin_devices web` runs the same visit in a browser on the operator's own laptop.** Three parts. (1) **The seam.** `visit.Console` already carried everything the wizard says and asks; the numbered-list rendering of `choose`, plus `title`, `note` and `enter`, move out of `Visit` and into it, so `Console` owns presentation and `Visit` owns the wizard. A front end that can draw a button overrides `choose` and is handed the index; one that cannot inherits the numbered list. `Visit` itself is otherwise untouched. (2) **`workin_devices/web.py`**: `WebConsole(visit.Console)` turns the wizard into typed events a page renders and answers, `Visit.run()` runs on a daemon thread, and an `http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer` built the way `capture.serve` builds one serves one page, a long-polled event stream, the answers, and five single-step tools. **Stop from the page raises `KeyboardInterrupt` inside the waiting question**, which is the only way to reach the wizard's own interrupted path: `SIGINT` is delivered to the main thread and the run is not on it. Stopping therefore writes the report, files the "stopped early" finding and asks the restore checklist **on the page**, as a single Ctrl-C does in a terminal. **That interrupt is one-shot** (round 3): the checklist's questions come through the same console after the interrupt is caught, so a flag that stayed set raised on every one of them and filed "the restore steps were not completed" even when the operator had done all of it. Ctrl-C in the command serving the page is the other case -- nobody is left at the page to answer -- so `Session.close` *abandons* the run, and then waits for the report and for any single step still writing a file. (3) **The tools row** -- read a terminal, back up its log, send `once`, check this laptop's network, scan the LAN -- runs one step against one address while no visit is running. `once` writes its config through `Visit.write_zk_agent_config`, newly extracted so the wizard and the button cannot write different files. An address may carry its port (`127.0.0.1:14370`), as the wizard's own "type the address" step already accepts. |
| Why | A visit is a linear terminal script that cannot repeat a step. On 2026-09-21 one lost ARP exchange at step 6 (D-274) ended a visit that had already read the terminal, taken its backup and allocated it, and the operator answered every question again from the beginning. The terminal also shows one line at a time: the transcript, the findings, the results sheet as it fills and the files written cannot be read together, which is where the operator's own judgement is supposed to come from. Neither is a defect in the wizard's logic, which is why the logic is not what changed. |
| Security | This process reads terminals on a customer's LAN and holds the lab's agent token, so the page is treated as a way in and closed accordingly: the listener binds **127.0.0.1 only**, and a `--host` whose addresses are not all loopback is refused before anything binds rather than documented as the operator's problem (round 2) -- bound anywhere else, terminal reads, the report downloads and lab-backed sends are reachable from the customer's LAN over plaintext with a URL token as the whole defence; every request but the page itself carries a token from `secrets.token_urlsafe`, invented per run, compared with `compare_digest` over bytes (a token that is not ASCII is a refusal, not a 500), carried in the address the command prints and **never written into the markup** -- though it is passed to `webbrowser.open`, which execs the browser with the address in `argv`, so on a laptop without `hidepid` another local user could read it from `/proc`; that is outside the stated threat model of one operator's own laptop and is named here rather than mitigated (round 3); a request whose `Origin` is present and is not loopback is refused, so a page the operator has open in another tab cannot drive this one; **an answer names the question it answers** and one that names a question the wizard has already left is refused (round 2) -- the same token URL open in two tabs otherwise lets a stale press land on whatever is waiting now, and a typed answer arriving at a choice prompt takes option 0, which on the consent prompt is yes; a download is reduced to its last path component and must still resolve inside `field-report`; **the standalone scan asks for the customer's permission**, as the runbook requires and the wizard does, rather than being a button that skips the question (round 2); the page loads nothing from anywhere else (`default-src 'none'`). What this deliberately does **not** add: no password and no TLS. On loopback, for one operator's own laptop, a per-run token is the proportionate control; anything reachable from a network would need both, which is why the non-loopback bind is refused instead of documented. |
| Also changed | `Console` gained `title`, `note`, `enter` and `choose`; `Visit`'s four matching methods now delegate presentation and keep only their logic. `tests/test_visit.py`'s `ScriptedConsole` inherits `visit.Console` -- **one line changed, and no other line of that file, which is the regression proof for the refactor**: `ScriptedConsole` overrides only `__init__`, `say`, `ask` and `text`, so it inherits `title`, `note`, `enter` and `choose` and every prompt assertion in the file exercises the moved rendering through the scripted seam. (This read "the other 1 459 are untouched" until review round 5. 1 459 was `main`'s line count; the file is over 2 000 here, because this branch is stacked on D-274's, which adds to it. The count was stale, not the claim.) `Visit.write_zk_agent_config` extracted from `agent_zk`. `Visit` keeps the in/out column it proved (`Visit.in_out`) instead of only writing it to the sheet, so a step repeated from a button sends on the column this visit established rather than a default (round 2). The address line is printed flushed: block-buffered through a pipe or a service log, the one line carrying the token would otherwise not appear until the process ended. |
| Not in this change | **No second way to do anything.** `visit` still runs the whole wizard in the terminal and is unchanged from the operator's side; the page is another front end onto it, not a fork of it. **No production path**: Mode A (the lab) only, as `visit` is. **No hosting**: this is not served to a network, and nothing here is a step towards that. **No page for the Hikvision or USB flows on their own** -- they run inside the wizard as they always have; only the five steps listed above are separately runnable. |
| Regression coverage | `tests/test_web.py`. `APageRunningAVisit`: the whole 4370 visit driven over HTTP against the emulator and `FakePlatform` -- the report and backup written, the sheet the page draws being the visit's own, `in_out_field` resolved, the LAN scanned once, and **`terminal.write_attempts == []`**, so the page reads a terminal and never writes to one; a choice arriving as the value behind the button rather than as its index, pinned on the one answer whose meaning is visible from outside (no consent, no scan); Stop ending the run with the wizard's own interrupted finding; a single step running alone, refused while a visit is running, and reporting an absent terminal instead of raising; an address carrying its port. `WhatThePageRefuses`: loopback-only bind; the page loading without a token and carrying none; **every other route refused without one, with the wrong one, with a truncated one and with a non-ASCII one**; three foreign origins refused and the page's own accepted; seven shapes of traversal refused and the legitimate name served; an unknown route answered rather than raising. `TheTranscriptThePageReads`: a page opened late served the run from its start, the console's three kinds reaching it as written, and a question that waits for the page with Stop raising where it waits. **Review round 2 on #319** reported seven findings against the tools row and the page's answer path, all accepted and fixed, with a test each. `APageRunningAVisit` gains the two-tab case: question 1 is answered, and the first tab's repeat of that same answer is refused with 409 while the consent prompt that replaced it stays unanswered, so the scan does not run. `WhatTheToolsMustNotAssume` covers the rest: the Comm Key, port and UDP the wizard discovered are reused by a repeated step for *that* address and not carried to another, while the page may still override them; a standalone `once` refuses to send until the in/out column is known, and takes the one this visit proved; a scan on a laptop with several networks asks which, narrows a large one to the /24 around this laptop exactly as the wizard does, refuses a large network this laptop is not on, and writes its `scan-*.json` where the wizard writes its own; and a visit cannot start while a tool still holds the terminal. `WhatTheWizardWaitsFor` pins the shutdown: an interrupted visit's report is on disk before `close()` returns, and `close()` reports false rather than claiming a visit that did not finish. **Before the fix**, against `web.py` at `34965f5b`: a stale typed answer reached the consent prompt and returned option 0 -- consent granted; `start()` returned `True` while a tool held the terminal; and `Session` had no `close()`, so the process could exit before the interrupted visit wrote its report. A second batch of three, on the same round: the bind check above, the scan's consent, and `once` no longer returning its findings in the response as well as writing them through the shared console -- the page drew every one of them twice, so one send read as two. Their tests: every non-loopback `--host` refused and `run` exiting 2 with the reason while four loopback spellings are accepted; a scan refused before consent with `probe.scan` set to raise if reached; and a standalone `once` whose response carries a count while the transcript carries the findings exactly once. Suite: **199 tests, one skipped** (`pyzk` absent), up from 99 -- this branch carries D-274's own round-2 to round-5 tests too, since it is stacked on it; `tests/test_web.py` is 58 of them. **This is the row kept current with the head.** Every round row below reports the suite **after that round's fixes landed** and names the head they landed on -- not the head that was reviewed, which is usually one commit earlier. A later count must never be written into one, which is exactly what happened when this row was the one that needed updating. Driven by hand against `sim-zk` in a browser as well: the tools row read the simulated terminal and wrote its backup, and the files panel linked it. |
